◈ FEED
WAR v71 Jul 2026
🔬 THE EXTENDED META-LAB STUDY — thousands more duels, hand-designed challengers, and a rock-paper-scissors upset
The book doubled in size and got pressure-tested from three directions at once. A second research round ran 60 more evolutionary runs (96 total across both studies), 5 hand-designed "manual challenger" doctrines built to test specific hypotheses about gaps in the champions, and a full round-robin tournament of book + AI + manual doctrines — 200+ pairings at 800 duels each (150,000+ duels), with every headline result re-verified at 6,000 duels for statistical confidence. The doctrine book grew from 12 entries to 18. Console: PROSPECT.LAB.explore({era,gens,pop}) to run your own search; every doctrine now carries an author tag (◆AI-discovered / ✎hand-designed / original) visible in the Prospect tab.
2030: the Inventor found a cleanly better answer. Patient Saturation refines Silent Saturation — drop aggression to exactly zero and reallocate the doctrine-tempo budget into hypersonic depth — and beats the original champion 65-67% head-to-head over 6,000 duels. Silent Saturation remains in the book as the historical champion; Patient Saturation is the new one.
2035: the first genuine peer rivalry the lab has measured. Dead Hand — zero aggression, maximum directed energy AND maximum swarm, nothing spent on maneuver — fights Shield-and-Lance to a dead-even 50/50 coin flip while crushing the rest of the field harder than the champion does. Neither doctrine has a reliable counter over the other; two legitimate top-tier answers now coexist at this horizon.
2040: no permanent champion — a measured rock-paper-scissors triangle. The original study called Tempo Sovereign uncounterable ("no reliable counter found"). The extended search found two: Glass Spear (drop directed energy to almost nothing, max out hypersonic strike) beats Tempo Sovereign 55%; Full Spectrum Vanguard (fund every axis at once within budget) loses to Tempo Sovereign but beats Glass Spear 74.5% — punishing the glass cannon's thin shield; and Tempo Sovereign beats Full Spectrum Vanguard back. A genuine intransitive cycle, confirmed live by the game's own PROSPECT.LAB.counterTable('2040'). Tempo Sovereign keeps the highest aggregate win rate across the whole field and remains the AI's default pick, but it is no longer unbeatable — exactly the situation the v70 live meta-adaptation system (commanders shift doctrine when they sense they're losing) was built to handle.
Five hand-designed doctrines tested specific hypotheses — most failed instructively. Quantum Panopticon and Absolute Zero bet that concentrated quantum-ISR investment could pierce the "everyone hides" meta; both lost 100% to every reigning champion. Orbital Overwatch tested the almost-entirely-unused orbital axis; also 100% losses. Gene-correlation analysis explains why: quantum/orbital investment only pays off past a threshold, and none of these builds crossed it — the budget spent got taken from swarm/DE/hyper, which have no such gate. Disciplined Blitz tested whether loud, concentrated, high-tempo maneuver warfare could win without the EMCON+dispersion "stealth tax" every champion pays; it lost 100% at every horizon and is now the book's third recorded failure — dispersion and EMCON are the single strongest predictors of win rate at every era (r=0.84-0.98). Layered Swarm (pairing top-tier directed energy with top-tier swarm mass) is the one hypothesis that earned a place in the book: a legitimate mid-tier hybrid that loses to the true champions but beats 2040's Glass Spear 80% by exploiting its thin self-defence.
WAR v70 Jul 2026
⚒ PROSPECT × THE INVENTOR — the meta lab: the AI breeds, tests and adopts the future of war
Prospect is now part sandbox, part simulator — and the AI plays it to win. The prospective layer no longer just fields future tech; the AI now adapts to the new weaponry, discovers the "new metas" each horizon creates, and adopts the best doctrine and employment of technology to pursue victory across every front. The Inventor's forge mechanic has been massively expanded into a full evolutionary meta lab on PROSPECT.LAB: it breeds employment genomes (aggression, EMCON discipline, dispersion, tech-bet depth, and per-technology reliance on autonomy/DE/swarms/quantum/hypersonics/orbital/doctrine) through mutation, crossover and survival-of-the-fittest across Monte-Carlo duels in each era's power landscape. Console: PROSPECT.LAB.explore({era:'2035'}) evolves a meta from scratch; PROSPECT.LAB.report('2040') prints the era's matchup table.
The lab models the TRADE-OFFS, so its answers are honest. Early lab builds "won" by turning every dial to maximum — so the duel engine was rebuilt around real tensions: a force-design budget (you cannot buy everything), EMCON self-blinding (running dark also dims your own kill-chain unless passive/quantum ISR compensates), concentration vs dispersion (massing wins fights and eats saturation salvos), and a maturity tax (betting beyond the era's proven tech means misfires — IFF fratricide, runaway swarms, hallucinated orders). After the rebuild the champions differentiated by era exactly as real force-design debates do.
📕 The doctrine book — twelve doctrines bred from 36 evolutionary runs and 1,800+ duels per era, written into the Prospect tab with battle notes quoting the lab's measured win rates. 2030: Silent Saturation (the champion — run dark, disperse, drown them in cheap airframes: 96% vs Ghost Lance, 100% vs Watchful Bastion), Ghost Lance, Steel Rain, and Watchful Bastion — a recorded 0% failure kept as a warning that pure defense concedes the meta. 2035: Shield-and-Lance (matured lasers blunt the swarm — beats 2030's champion 97%, the book's cleanest counter-meta story), Kill-Web Rush, Mirage Legion, Quiet Depths (a quantum-ISR specialist). 2040: Tempo Sovereign (the transparent-battlefield champion — hiding is dead, win the OODA war), Lance Storm (its only measured answer, 33%), Proven Hand (the professional's floor — never embarrassed, never decisive), and Icarus Gambit — the second recorded failure: a 1.0 bet on unproven everything, 0% across 1,800+ duels. The future must be bought at the rate it matures.
⚒ Live meta-adaptation in battle. With prospect on, each commander opens with the book doctrine that fits his personality (aggressive commanders reach for aggressive metas, cunning ones for EMCON and quantum ISR) — and when he senses he is losing the meta fight (power trend collapsing, belief picture blind, misfires biting), the Inventor's field response kicks in: he shifts to the lab's measured counter to the enemy's doctrine. Stubborn commanders cling to dying metas (the personality gate), shifts carry a cooldown and a 3-shift limit, and every opening and shift is logged to the feed and the Prospect tab's live panel. Doctrine adoption drives the real engine: side tactics, per-domain doctrines, emission discipline, swarm and hypersonic employment.
Eleven new prospective systems join the capability tree, each wired into real mechanics: AI logistics command (predictive resupply), deep-magazine arsenal ships, railgun / hypervelocity artillery, EW decoy/jammer swarms (phantom tracks for the enemy belief engine), UUV wolfpacks, autonomous ground vehicles, on-orbit servicing/repair (constellations self-heal faster), counter-hypersonic glide interceptors (thins the uninterceptable leakers), resilient mesh C2 (comms-loss immunity), cognitive-EW adaptive jamming, and orbital fires cueing — bringing the tree to 32 capabilities across all seven domains, every one carrying era, maturity tier, reliability and ideology note.
FIXED: one doctrine per DOMAIN per side. The doctrine picker no longer allows only a single doctrine per color — each side now sets a Combined-arms doctrine plus independent Land, Air and Naval overrides (naval appears when the force fields ships). Every per-unit doctrine read in the engine — combat matchups, morale doctrine bonuses, posture and targeting — resolves through the unit's domain slot first, falling back to the side-wide doctrine, so an infantry brigade can fight under Defense-in-Depth while the air wing flies SEAD/DEAD and the fleet runs Distributed Lethality.
WAR v69 Jul 2026
🔬 WARVAL — a validation suite that tests the engine against real history
Code-accessible, never on screen. A rigorous, headless test harness lives on window.WARVAL — it renders nothing, touches no game state, and never runs on its own. Open the console and type WARVAL.run(). It exists purely to answer one question honestly: does the engine actually reproduce how real wars ended, or only in theory?
Ten real conflicts, run 1:1 against history. Gulf War, Vietnam, Korea, Soviet–Afghanistan, WWII, Russia–Ukraine, Falklands, the Six-Day War, Iran–Iraq and the Winter War — each declared with quantified inputs (force ratios, tech overmatch, war scale, aims, regime type, terrain, insurgency) and its documented historical ending type and winner. WARVAL runs each hundreds of Monte-Carlo times, classifies how the engine ended it (decisive rout / negotiated stalemate / home-front political exit / economic collapse / attritional grind / insurgent bleed), and compares the distribution to history. Current result: 10 / 10 conflicts reproduced, 100% fidelity — the Gulf and Six-Day wars end as decisive routs, Vietnam and Afghanistan as insurgent bleeds that break the occupier’s will, Korea and the Winter War as negotiated limited outcomes, WWII as economic/coalition collapse, Ukraine and Iran–Iraq as grinding attrition.
It tests the REAL engine, and tracks drift across updates. The tactical layer calls the engine’s own combat-matchup function and unit tables; the strategic layer pulls the calibrated home-front resilience model — change the balance and the fidelity score moves with it. WARVAL.snapshot('v69') stores a baseline and WARVAL.diff('v69') reports exactly which conflicts a later update improved or regressed. Also: WARVAL.run({trials,only}) and WARVAL.list(). (Building it immediately caught real calibration gaps — an over-fast economic-collapse rate and a too-strict home-front-collapse gate — which were then fixed.)
⌁ PROSPECT — a framework for fighting the next war
⌁ Prospect tab (off by default — the base game is untouched until you enable it). A scaffold for future-proofing strategy: turn it on and the battle is re-fought with the emerging tech, tactics and ideology of the wars to come. Pick a horizon — 2030 / 2035 / 2040 — and how far out on the maturity curve you’ll bet: Fielded → Prototype → Experimental → Unproven → Concept → Black Project.
Twenty-one capabilities across seven domains — 🤖 Autonomous Systems (loyal-wingman UCAVs → human-out-of-the-loop hunters → fully autonomous AI command), ⚡ Directed Energy (laser CIWS → high-power microwave → space-based DE), 🐝 Swarming (attritable swarms → 1,000-drone self-organizing swarms → bio-hybrid), ⚛ Quantum ISR (quantum magnetometers → quantum radar that ends stealth → total networked ISR), 🚀 Hypersonics (boost-glide → scramjet cruise → hypersonic swarm salvos), 🛰 Orbital Warfare (proliferated-LEO custody → co-orbital kill vehicles → FOBS bombardment), and 📖 Emerging Doctrine (multi-domain ops → mosaic kill-webs → cognitive/algorithmic warfare). Each wires into the real systems: quantum ISR sharpens the belief engine and defeats stealth; directed energy burns down drone swarms and stiffens missile-raid interception; hypersonics punch uninterceptable leakers through the salvo defence; autonomy makes forces immune to morale break; swarming fields attritable mass.
The framework models the RISK of betting on the future, not just the promise. Every capability carries a reliability — and the deeper the bet, the lower it runs. Unproven and black-project systems misfire: autonomous hunters suffer IFF fratricide, mega-swarms go runaway, AI command hallucinates orders a human never would, black-project weapons fail to cue. Each also carries an ideology note, and the horizon rolls up into a doctrine profile — 2030’s human-on-the-loop multi-domain convergence, 2035’s human-out-of-the-loop mosaic kill-web, 2040’s AI-commanded transparent battlefield where the fight moves to the decision loop itself.
Built to extend. The whole thing is a data-driven registry — PROSPECT.register({id,name,domain,era,tier,rel,effect,ideology}) adds a capability in one line, ready for future updates to grow the next-war tech tree.
WAR v68 Jul 2026
🛰 The Orbital Domain — space becomes a system every other system leans on
Space is no longer a bag of assets — it is a contested domain with a per-side order of battle. Each side now fields seven real constellation types, health-rated and scaled by national quality: 📷 EO recon (daylight imaging, weather-blocked), 📡 SAR radar-imaging (all-weather, sees through cloud and night), 📶 ELINT/SIGINT (geolocates enemy emitters), 🔥 early-warning IR (SBIRS-class launch detection), 🛰 GNSS/PNT (GPS/GLONASS/Galileo), 📻 SATCOM, and 🌦 weather sats — plus a shared 🌍 Starlink-class mega-constellation. Read the whole picture on the new 🛰 Space tab.
Everything ties into everything. Satellites are not scenery — they feed the war: SAR & EO passes drop high-quality tracks straight into the v67 belief engine (SAR works in the weather that blinds EO); ELINT sats geolocate emitters into the SIGINT picture; early-warning sats add interception capacity to saturation missile raids (reaction time); recon sats cue the fleet's cruise missiles over the horizon — a blinded navy with no satellite and no local track holds its fire; GNSS health drives guided-munition accuracy; and SATCOM + Starlink hold the C2 net together. Shoot the enemy's constellations down and he goes blind across all of it.
🌍 Starlink, modelled both ways it really cuts. A side that leans on the mega-constellation gets a resilient comms backbone and a bistatic passive-radar bonus — faint persistent tracks skimmed off the reflections of thousands of downlinks, fed into its belief picture. But those same terminals emit on the uplink: using Starlink lights your own formations up on the enemy's ELINT, handing him SIGINT tracks of your positions. Using the enemy's internet as your radar — and paying for your own use in emissions — exactly as the real debate runs.
◇ Ultra-high-altitude ISR platforms. Capable sides launch a real U-2 / RQ-4 Global Hawk / stratospheric balloon — an actual unit on the map, flying far above the air battle with enormous sensors feeding the belief engine continuously. It survives the way the real thing does — altitude and low observability, not armor — so it persists until the enemy commits air superiority deep into the rear to kill it (à la the 2019 Global Hawk shootdown). Lose it and a hole opens in your picture. Militias don't field them (the discipline gate).
☄ Anti-satellite combat & the Kessler price
ASAT weaponry — four ways to kill a satellite, each gated by Space Domain Awareness (you must track a bird to shoot it) and orbital reach (only capable nations get there): direct-ascent kinetic (a missile from the ground — devastating, but it breeds debris), co-orbital killer (a shadowing inspector sat that disables in orbit — clean and deniable), directed-energy dazzle (a ground laser that temporarily blinds EO optics), and cyber intrusion into the ground station (the soft underbelly — hijack the downlink). Commanders reach for ASAT when the enemy's space edge is hurting them, and it climbs the strategic escalation ladder.
☄ Kessler syndrome — the tragedy of the commons in orbit. Every kinetic ASAT kill spews a debris cloud that raises a global Kessler index — and that debris degrades every low-orbit constellation for BOTH sides (EO, SAR, ELINT, weather, Starlink), the shooter's included. Debris slowly de-orbits over time, but a war fought with kinetic ASAT blinds everyone. The Space tab shows the live debris level and the per-constellation health lost to it.
☢ High-altitude nuclear EMP — the catastrophe option. A losing side, deep on the escalation ladder, may detonate a nuke in the upper atmosphere: a theatre-wide electromagnetic pulse that scrambles every satellite and radio at once (all constellations to a quarter strength for a spell) and jolts the debris field. Rare, AI-gated, and a hard escalation — the Starfish Prime nightmare.
🔓 Cyber update — the ground segment is the front line
Cyber and space are now one fight. On top of the existing cyber suite (C2 intrusion, ISR spoofing, logistics attack, AD suppression, GPS/SATCOM jamming), the space layer adds the modern reality that the weakest link in a satellite is its ground station: cyber ASAT hijacks a constellation's downlink without ever reaching orbit, GPS spoofing (distinct from jamming — it sends the enemy's guided munitions to the wrong grid rather than merely denying them), and responsive-space reconstitution lets a damaged constellation slowly relaunch and self-heal toward its baseline. Space Domain Awareness is itself computed from your live sensors and ELINT — blind yourself and you can't even find the targets to shoot.
Layered & guarded, integrates with the legacy space layer. The orbital domain runs alongside the v48 C4ISR recon-satellite passes and the v49 Command-Fabric constellations rather than replacing them; it is rebuilt each battle, throttled, and fully try/caught — if anything throws, every existing system continues unchanged and the sim never freezes.
WAR v67 Jul 2026
🛰 The Information & Belief Engine — fog of war becomes a system
Information is now a resource, not a fact. Until now a sensor detecting a unit meant the commander instantly, perfectly knew where it was. That is gone. The new pipeline is: raw multi-modal sensing → imperfect OBSERVATIONS → up the chain of command (latency & loss) → FUSION at the commander (weighted by trust) → BELIEF TRACKS with confidence, not certainty → decay & disinformation → the commander plans on that believed picture, so he can be wrong. The trigger-puller still shoots what he can physically see (ground-truth contact is unchanged — combat is untouched); it is the commander's picture that is now a belief that can be stale, incomplete, or salted with ghosts.
Reports climb the chain — and don't always arrive. Every observation is tagged with the reporting unit's HQ and routed upward with a latency set by that HQ's C2 integrity: good comms deliver in well under a second; a shattered or jammed HQ delivers 4–6s late (the report is already stale when the commander reads it) or loses it entirely. Verified in play: a side under EW routinely drops 15–40 reports to comms/jamming per engagement, and its picture visibly lags reality.
Confidence, not certainty — and human mistakes. The commander fuses arriving reports into tracks, each carrying a confidence, a position-error radius, a class guess (which may be "unknown"), and a strength estimate. Multiple sensors corroborating a track sharpen it; a lone weak report stays uncertain. The AI's battlefield read now uses the believed enemy strength, anchored on the rough order of battle he knows going in but distorted by his picture: a blinded commander slightly under-counts and turns over-confident; a deceived one over-counts and turns over-cautious — a plausible human band, never catastrophically wrong.
Sensor trust that adapts. Each commander holds a per-modality trust level (👁 visual, 📡 radar, 🌡 thermal, 🔊 acoustic, 📶 SIGINT). When a track is confirmed by reality, the sensor that fed it gains trust; when a track turns out to be a ghost, that sensor loses it. Jamming teaches a side to distrust its own radar within seconds — watch radar trust collapse and SIGINT/thermal take over on the ISR tab.
Disinformation & the D-Day problem. Real reports can be drowned in false ones. Every sensor throws occasional false positives (clutter, thermal ghosts, jamming artefacts — more under EW and bad weather), and a strategic deception operation (the ⚡ Strategic tab lever) now plants phantom decoy formations directly onto the enemy commander's tactical belief picture — a fake army on the net he may commit reserves against. Information warfare finally bites where it should: in what the enemy believes.
📡 The Sensor Overhaul — real detection physics
Five modalities, each modelled honestly (the best one wins each look; corroboration happens at fusion):
👁 Visual — needs line of sight; gutted at night (×0.45) and by fog/smoke; reads the target's visual signature. Precise position, excellent classification — but short-legged and weather-bound.
📡 Radar — models the radar horizon from earth curvature: a low or ground target beyond the horizon (a function of both the sensor's and target's height) is simply gone, while an aircraft is visible far out — so ground forces stay hidden at range until they close, exactly as in life. Rain attenuates it hard; reads radar cross-section (stealth airframes are dim, submerged submarines are invisible to it). Precise — but an active radar RADIATES, and that emission is detectable…
🌡 Thermal — models thermal-crossover layers: contrast collapses in mid-day heat and sharpens at night and in snow, so thermals are a night sensor. Sees hot engine signatures, penetrates smoke and haze that blind the eye. Medium precision.
🔊 Acoustic — needs no line of sight (sound travels around hills); a cold still night carries it far, a storm scatters it. Hears loud things — artillery firing, armor moving — but is bearing-only, so it produces large-error "something loud over there" contacts. This is how you first learn a battery is out there without ever seeing it.
📶 SIGINT — passive: detects enemy emissions — every active radar, every EW jammer, every unit that just fired lights up the electromagnetic spectrum and can be located from far off. This is the counter-weight to radar: emitting is never free, and a jammer is the loudest thing on the battlefield. Emissions are listed live on the ISR tab.
Electronic emission signatures & per-modality weather attenuation — every unit carries a signature per modality; weather now attenuates each sensor differently (fog wrecks the eye but barely touches radar; rain wrecks radar and acoustics; a clear cold night is the thermal/acoustic sweet spot). The two systems intertwine: a jammer blinds the enemy's radar and eyes, inflates his false-positive rate and position errors — while screaming its own location to his SIGINT.
🛰 The ISR tab (new, readable)
A whole new bottom-deck tab. Per side: a plain-language fusion-cell summary ("holds 12 tracks — 10 real, 2 phantom; picture accuracy 83%; believes enemy power 156 vs true 183 — under-estimating 15%; under EW jamming"), adaptive sensor-trust bars, and the report-flow ledger (in transit / delivered / lost to comms & EW / false positives). Below: the viewed side's track table (class, contributing modalities, position-error radius, confidence, age), the emissions/SIGINT picture, and a running intel event log. A toggle draws the belief overlay on the map: every track as an estimated position with a confidence-graded uncertainty ring — phantoms and decoys dashed in amber — so you literally see the difference between where the enemy is and where your commander thinks he is.
Layered & guarded. The whole engine is rebuilt each battle and fully try/caught; if any part throws, the legacy per-side spotting continues unchanged and the sim never freezes. Sensing runs on its own throttle (0.4s) with a per-side pair budget so one large force can't starve the other side's ISR net.
WAR v66 Jul 2026
⚓ The Naval Overhaul — the fleet joins the war
Real systems at real scaled ranges. Classes rebuilt from published specifications (Mk 45 5"/62 gun ~24 km · Harpoon 130–310 km · SM-2/6 area SAMs 240–460 km · Tomahawk ~1,600 km · Mk 48 torpedo ~50 km · carrier air wing combat radius ~720 km). At this map's scale (land artillery = 30): warships' base range is now 32 — the gunline properly outranges tube artillery from offshore; ship-launched land-attack cruise missiles reach the entire map; torpedoes are short-ranged (16) but ship-killers.
The 3D domain — carriers above, submarines below. ⊞ Aircraft Carrier (CVN): a 100k-ton mobile airfield assigned automatically to any 4+-hull fleet — friendly aircraft within its ~45u service radius rearm and refuel alongside (its own armament is point-defence only; protect it). ⊛ Submarine: runs submerged — only aircraft overhead or warships close enough for a sonar solution (<14u) can engage it; guns and land fires cannot touch it; launching torpedoes or cruise missiles unmasks the boat for ~9s. ▣ Assault Ship (LHD): closes with a coastline and puts marine platoons and amtracs into the water, lift by lift.
Naval support to the land battle. Destroyers/cruisers/frigates project a SAM umbrella ~30u over the littoral — friendly troops under it are measurably harder for enemy aircraft to hit (the SM-2/6 pattern). DDGs, CGs and SSNs run deliberate cruise-missile launch cycles against high-value land targets: enemy artillery, missile launchers, EW, air defences and logistics. Naval gunfire (the range-32 main batteries) pounds the beach in direct support.
Naval support to the strategic war. Coastal sectors within reach of reserve naval power get a carrier group offshore when their battle is rendered (+2 sorties and a naval gunline), and SEALIFT: a coastal sector supplied by a fleet in being is never fully cut off — supply throughput floors at 75% past any severed land MSR. Guided naval munitions already ride the existing GPS/PNT satellite state, tying the fleet into the space layer.
Fleet composition — capital ships are never random rolls (weight 0 in the subtype table); they're assigned by fleet logic at spawn, so the Naval & Air scenario now reliably fields opposing carrier battle groups with escorts and a submarine each, and Beach Landing fields a proper amphibious task force (gunline + CVN + LHD).
⚔ Combined Arms — the branches fight as one
SEAD before strike packages (the air gate). Built on joint SEAD doctrine (MCWP 3-22.2: suppression aircraft lead; everything behind them depends on it). When the enemy has a live, layered AD net (3+ SAM/AAA emitters, including SAM ships) and you have the means to suppress it, your strike aircraft hold at the push point — only SEAD jets and pure air-to-air work inside the envelope. The gate lifts when the net is worked down below 3 emitters ("corridor open — push") or when the commander's patience runs out (15–45s scaled by aggression: "accepts the SAM risk"). Verified: an 11-emitter net gates BLUE's strikers within 2 scan cycles, and both lift paths fire.
Supported advance (the ground gate). Infantry and armor moving into ground where local enemy power exceeds 1.35× their own support hold short and wait for air cover when their side has aircraft up — advancing at a crawl until fast-movers are within ~32u or the commander's patience (18–32s by aggression) expires and they go without it. Commanders announce holds and releases on the net.
Conventional ≠ asymmetric (the discipline gate). Both gates apply only to professional forces: a side's discipline is computed live from its troops' individual skill/gear plus commander experience. Below the threshold — a militia — there is no ATO and no fire-support net: they swarm, exactly as the v65 asymmetric scenarios intend. The two kinds of war now genuinely fight differently.
⛺ Battle Framing — wars are fought over someone's ground
The defender defends its home ground. War-sector battles read territory control: past 58/42 the owning side defends in prepared positions — ~60% of its combat units dug in on the objectives (+cover, +morale for fighting at home), the rest in depth across its half, fires and logistics in the rear — while the attacker mounts a deliberate assault from its line of departure. Contested sectors (control ≈ 50) remain classic meeting engagements, and ordinary skirmishes are untouched.
Attacker intel opens the deep battle. The attacker's intelligence picture (commander quality + SOF capacity) gates two openers: at intel > 55%, SOF teams (callsigned, Tier-1) are already operating in the defender's rear when the battle starts; at intel > 40% with air available, an airborne drop puts up to 3 sticks behind the forward line. Verified live: an 85%-intel BLUE assault opened with 2 SOF teams deep and 3 paradropped squads mid-map.
☄ Saturation Warfare — the thousand-missile problem
Raids now arrive in real numbers. Modern saturation attacks are dozens-to-hundreds of airframes at once (Iran→Israel Apr 2024: ~300+ drones/missiles, ~99% stopped). The new salvo system resolves each raid statistically against the defender's layered interception capacity (interceptors, SAM batteries, AAA, MANPADS, EW soft-kill, Aegis ships), draws a representative skyful of tracks, and lands the leakers as real impacts. Big raids always leak a little (~1.5% floor); a saturated or attrited net leaks catastrophically. Live counters (raids / inbound / intercepted / leakers) on the Live tab.
Missile Defence rebuilt — single off-map missiles replaced by 24–80+ missile raids on a cadence; the defender now spawns a proper layered network (5 SAM batteries + MANPADS teams). Verified: ~97% interception with a healthy net over 100–235-missile campaigns — and it degrades honestly as batteries die.
Drone Swarm rebuilt — waves every ~16s up to 9 waves, each larger than a normal battlefield's whole force; real airframes spawn to a performance ceiling (~190 units) and the rest of each launch package resolves through the salvo system, so a wave reads "Wave 3: 132 airframes launched" and means it.
Fixes & UI
Per-sector doctrines (both sides). A new Sector Doctrines panel on the war setup screen: BLUE picks any doctrine (all 16, from Blitzkrieg to SEAD/DEAD Package) per sector; RED's commander auto-assigns per sector from terrain + temperament (defense in the mountains, blitzkrieg on the plain, asymmetric in the cities). Applied whenever that sector's battle is fought; side defaults restore at war's end.
Voicelines you can actually see and hear. They previously went only to the scrolling ticker/feed (easy to miss entirely). Now: a radio overlay floats over the top of the map — big type, side colour, fades after ~5s — and lines are spoken aloud via the browser's built-in speech synthesis (fully local, distinct voice per side: BLUE crisp, RED deep). The 🎙 button cycles VOICE → TEXT → OFF. New line pools for the new doctrine moments: SEAD holds, corridor-open calls, air-cover waits, cruise-missile launches, airborne drops, saturation raids.
NaN veterancy (pre-existing since the stat was added) — supply trucks and EW jammers have zero weapon damage, so the spawn-time quality formula divided 0/0 = NaN, silently poisoning every force's "avg veterancy" stat (and, since v65, those units' skill stat). Guarded.
Live tab deepened — new Combined-Arms Picture (battle frame + attacker intel, per-side discipline %, air-gate state, units holding for air, AD launchers up), Naval Picture (hull count, SAM ships, CVN/LHD/SSN status incl. submerged/exposed, aircraft cycling on the carrier deck, cruise missiles fired, marine lifts ashore), and the Air & Missile Defence raid ledger.
WAR v65 Jul 2026
Asymmetric Warfare — skill, gear & the small war
Individual skill & gear, game-wide. Every unit in every mode now carries two personal stats set at spawn: skill (marksmanship/fieldcraft, 0–1 — from national quality, subtype and the luck of who you got; feeds accuracy directly, an operator vs a conscript is worth ±10 points of hit chance) and gear (tier 0 improvised / 1 standard / 2 top-tier — tier 2 night vision cancels most of the darkness penalty, and infantry body armor reduces damage taken). The asymmetric scenarios push these to the extremes; ordinary battles feel them as texture.
✚ Downed Bird — a Mogadishu-1993-pattern raid gone wrong: a handful of Tier-1 operators with callsigns (a named callsign going down is an event on the feed) hold a crash site at the center of a hostile city while militia waves — technicals, iron sights, endless numbers — pour in from every direction. Casualty-sensitive victory: lose more than half the operators and no body count redeems the mission; hold until the relief column at T+110s.
◙ Night Compound — a Benghazi-2012-pattern annex defence, always fought at night: NVGs, plates and marksmanship on the rooftops against militia assault waves out of the dark — and mortars that take most of the night to find the range, exactly as they historically did. Verified across repeated runs to be a knife-edge hold: usually the annex holds, sometimes the waves get through early.
⌖ FPV Ambush — the Ukraine-2022–24 / civil-war asymmetry: a conventional armored column pushes into ground held by irregulars with dug-in AT teams, jammers, and FPV drone waves that keep coming (fresh drones every ~20s — they're cheap). Victory by blunting the armor: kill 60% of the column's vehicles before your own force breaks.
Militia reinforcement waves — Downed Bird and Night Compound stream fresh RED fighters in from the map edges on a cadence, so the defence never runs out of targets — or of trouble.
Amphibious Combat — game-wide foundation
Water is now a contested medium, not a wall. Any ground unit in any mode can enter water: infantry swim/take assault craft (slow), IFV/APC/recon vehicles are amphib-rated and swim best, tanks ford painfully, artillery barge-crawls. While in the water a unit fires at −15 accuracy and takes +35% damage — crossing under fire is possible and bloody, exactly as it should be. This is the movement/exposure foundation for the larger naval & combined-arms overhaul.
Latent stuck-in-water freeze fixed — the old movement multipliers were a hard 0.0 on water cells, so any ground unit whose pathing carried it one step into water was frozen there forever (it could never move out because its speed was multiplied to zero at its current position). The new amphibious multipliers are small but non-zero, so units wade out instead of freezing.
≋ Beach Landing scenario — a dedicated coastal map (western ocean, surf line, beach, rising ground): naval gunline offshore, amtracs swimming in, infantry wading the surf under registered artillery fire. Win by establishing a beachhead (ground force firmly ashore + the defence broken); lose the landing in the water.
🎙 Commander Voicelines (fun mode)
Commanders now talk. A toggleable voiceline system (on by default — 🎙 button under the speed controls) has commanders call out on the ticker and feed at real moments: the opening address at engage, first contact, every plan change the cognitive AI actually makes (frontal assault, flank, artillery prep, defence, pause each have their own lines), a rally cry when their force's cohesion breaks, victory and defeat addresses — and a casualty call when a named operator goes down. Line choice is flavored by the speaking commander's personality: aggressive commanders bark ("Audacity. Always audacity."), cautious ones steady the line ("Slow is smooth, smooth is fast."). Purely cosmetic, zero simulation effect, rate-limited so it stays fun.
WAR v64 Jul 2026
Bug Audit & Fixes
The war couldn't actually be paused. The theatre war clock (warTicker) ran on its own requestAnimationFrame loop and never once checked a pause flag — the existing "⏸ Hold" control only ever froze a single rendered battle, not supply, reinforcement, counterattacks or the strategic instruments ticking underneath it. A real theatre-wide pause now exists: see War Options below.
Manual Deploy was silently dead since v52. The per-sector weight/formation editor looped over WAR.nodes, which is only populated once beginWar() runs — on the pre-war setup screen (where the editor is shown) it was always empty, so switching to MANUAL rendered zero rows and nothing was ever editable. It now reads the six-sector list straight from the selected theater, which is known before the war begins; weight and formation choices are verified flowing correctly into the opening force mix (confirmed: an Armored Spearhead sector at 4× weight fielded a veh/inf ratio over 6× that of a lightly-weighted Infantry Screen sector from the same pool).
Header version had drifted again. The title bar read "v51" while the Notes tab was already up to v63 — the same class of drift the v49 notes once fixed. Both now agree.
Harmless CSP console warning removed. frame-ancestors was declared on the page's <meta> Content-Security-Policy tag, where browsers ignore it and log a warning every load; the directive does nothing there in a locally-opened file with no framing surface to protect, so it's dropped.
Pause Mid-War
⏸ PAUSE WAR / ▶ RESUME WAR — a new control on the War tab (next to ◆ FRONT MAP and ✕ END WAR) that freezes the entire theatre: every sector's supply, reinforcement, counterattack and strategic-instrument ticking stops, and if you're currently commanding a rendered battle it freezes in lockstep too (re-entering a sector while paused keeps it frozen). A blinking ⏸ PAUSED marker shows in the War tab header and on the front-map overlay so it's never ambiguous whether the war is actually running.
More Instruments — ⚡ Strategic tab
Naval Blockade — a sustained posture gated by reserve naval power that strangles the enemy's war economy at sea: slower than an air campaign but far cheaper on legitimacy. An enemy fleet in being contests it and blunts the drain.
Cyber Offensive — a one-shot strike on the enemy's command network, cheaper and faster than a SOF raid: on success it jams their C2, dents their SOF capacity, and wipes any live target designation; a detected intrusion costs the initiator legitimacy and hardens the target's resolve instead.
Rally the Nation — spend legitimacy immediately for a war-economy surge and a resolve bump, trading political capital for tempo instead of waiting on passive regeneration.
RED wields all three — the strategic AI director now rolls naval blockade, cyber offensive and national rallies into its weighted instrument choice alongside the existing SOF/IO/deception/air-campaign toolkit, gated by the same archetype traits and shown restraint the same way (standing a blockade down when legitimacy craters).
War Setup — More Icons
Theater icons on the setup screen's theater selector (◈ Generic, ⚑ Western Europe, ░ North African Desert, ❄ Eastern Front, ⛩ Korean Peninsula) alongside the existing per-sector terrain glyphs.
Formation icons — each Deployment Plan formation archetype (⬡ Balanced, ◼ Armored Spearhead, ▲ Infantry Screen, ⊞ Artillery Heavy, ◆ Air Cavalry) now carries a glyph in both the dropdown and the manual per-sector row, and sector rows show their terrain glyph too.
⚔ Order of Battle preview — a new icon strip on the setup screen showing both sides' theatre-pool composition (▲ inf · ◼ veh · ◆ air · ⊞ arty · ⬡ naval · ⬟ drones) at the current front scale, and a ⛨ marker on the historical-commander blurbs, so the setup screen reads as a proper mission briefing before ⚔ BEGIN WAR.
AAR — Deepened, with an Agentic AI Overview
⚙ Agentic AI Overview — a new AAR section, per side: the commander's archetype and full trait profile, how many cognitive decision cycles it actually ran this engagement and the resulting plan distribution, its confidence/stress/fatigue arc from opening to close (narrated, not just numbers), what it learned this fight (memory-weight deltas on breakthrough/flank/artillery/defense biases that carry into its next battle), and its read of the enemy (the opponent model — flanking/artillery/retreat frequencies — that fed its counter-risk pricing). None of this was invented for the report; it's the commander agent's own running state, surfaced.
⏱ Decision Timeline — both sides' cognitive-cycle history merged and sorted, showing every plan chosen with the confidence/stress reading at the moment it was picked.
⟳ Tactical Adaptation — every mid-battle doctrine switch the ADAPT system triggered, with the from/to doctrine, the power ratio at the time, and the trigger reason.
⬡ Chain of Command — final HQ integrity and field-commander name/archetype for every division, so a decapitated HQ or a lucky field commander shows up in the debrief instead of only in the live Command panel.
WAR v63 Jul 2026
The Foundry — genuine invention (toggle-gated)
⚒ INVENTOR MODE (off by default — the base game is untouched while off). A toggle in the WORLD tab opens The Foundry: the Inventor stops choosing from a notebook of six schemes and starts inventing new mechanics. He composes effect primitives — an instruction set, not a menu: SACRIFICE (destroy your own assets to power an effect), OBSTACLE (persistent barriers), ZONE (denial fields, sensor nets, kill-zones, sanctuaries), COUPLE (reactive when-this-then-that automation), CONVERT (repurpose one force type into another at a loss), DOCTRINE_SHIFT (novel combined-arms pairings with real synergy), TEMPO (operational-rhythm deception) and SIGNAL (perception warfare against the enemy leader’s estimates).
Problem-driven, so invention has quality, not just novelty. Each cycle the Foundry diagnoses the war — chokepoint under pressure, armor fighting screenless, a losing C2 battle, starving intelligence, being outmassed, a bleeding economy, a wavering home front — and forges an answer to the top problem. A pressured narrows may get a blockship barrier: scuttle a fraction of your own fleet to close the strait. A losing C2 battle gets a bespoke reactive cyber-ISR system (a sensor net coupled to automatic jamming pulses). Screenless armor gets a new combined-arms doctrine. The mad options are genuinely on the table.
Costed, budgeted, cabinet-gated, and safe. Every invention must cost something (sacrificed forces, economy, escalation, political capital) and passes hard budgets: bounded magnitudes and durations, at most 3 live inventions per side, and the cabinet can veto expensive schemes like any other directive. The inventing intelligence only ever emits a blueprint — data, never code — interpreted by deterministic engine machinery.
Invented mechanics become heritable doctrine. An invention that demonstrably pays off is inscribed in the Doctrine Book together with its full blueprint — and in later wars the Foundry can re-forge proven inventions, adapted to the new war’s diagnosed problems. Your best inventions stop being lucky strokes and become the art of war.
Both sides invent. The enemy’s Foundry is as open as yours — expect to face barriers, kill-zones and bespoke systems you’ve never seen, announced in the ledger as they’re unveiled, and listed live in the WORLD tab.
WAR v62 Jul 2026
War Finance, Victory Alignment & the Experimental Edge
Keynesian war debt — total war no longer hits a wall; it levers up. A mobilised state whose economy would buckle now borrows instead: the fiscal signal is decoupled from the real burn, production runs on credit past the point raw stability allows — a bet that victory will retroactively justify the spending. Debt suppresses your economic ceiling, charges service, and over-leverage risks a confidence crisis. At war’s end the bet resolves: victory redeems the debt; defeat brings the reckoning with the peace. Float war bonds for an immediate production surge bought on credit — the ledger lives in the WORLD tab.
Tactical victories now mean something to the world. Every sector won lifts the victor’s home front, coalition and legitimacy, dents the loser’s, and moves the negotiation calculus — the beaten start thinking of terms, the winning stop. Both heads of state journal their battles, so the strategic layer and the front finally speak the same language.
⚗ Experimental mode (off by default — the base game is untouched). A trigger in the WORLD tab unlocks near-future bleeding-edge systems: hypersonic strikes no defence can answer, autonomous swarm release (machines hunting without a human in the loop), AI command fusion, cyber blackouts, and orbital reconstellation. Powerful, escalatory — and unstable by design: expect IFF failures and hallucinated orders.
WAR v61 Jul 2026
The Overlord Architecture — a strategic-AI paradigm shift
Heads of state now lead the war. Each side is led by a persona — one of five archetypes (Statesman, Gambler, Ideologue, Technocrat, Warlord) with real risk/reward thresholds, patience, ambition, paranoia and statecraft. The same war under a different leader is a different war: this is personality, not optimisation. Generals still command the front; the leader commands the war.
A government to please. Every leader answers to a cabinet & assembly — approval tracks the home front, the economy and the war’s progress; hawks and doves weight what passes; politically-costly directives get vetoed; and a collapsing government issues a binding peace mandate. Autocrats answer to an inner circle, democracies to an assembly — the leash lengths differ.
Ministers — sub-strategic AIs for every branch. Domestic, Logistics, Combined Arms, Army, Air, Economy, Diplomacy — each proposes directives in its own domain each cycle. And THE INVENTOR: an idea engine that proposes unconventional, sometimes completely backwards schemes (Reverse Deception, Economic Judo, the Silent Week…). Schemes that work are inscribed permanently in a Doctrine Book that survives across wars and seeds future planning; schemes that fail are quietly shelved.
Strategic fog, memory and assumptions. Leaders see their own house truly but the enemy only as estimates — error shrinks with command/ISR quality, and paranoid leaders systematically overestimate the foe. When confidence is thin they log explicit working assumptions and act on them. Each keeps a campaign journal and an opponent model — the enemy’s aggression, whether they retaliate in kind, the grudges — that persists through the war and shapes deterrence choices.
Emergent learning. Every executed directive’s outcome is measured against the war’s trajectory and fed back into that action’s value. Adaptability gates the update — the Technocrat learns fast, the Ideologue barely learns at all. The uncontrolled side plays the full architecture live; the old scripted RED reflexes are superseded — the overlord assumes command.
The chain of command, complete. Overlord → cabinet gate → ministers → a central executor that turns directives into the existing national levers (scale, aims, campaigns, SOF, diplomacy, readiness) feeding down to general command. The overlord also exploits black swans — reading each world shock for the opening it creates.
👑 CABINET tab. Your council in full — persona, grand plan, cabinet approval, opponent model, journal, learned preferences — plus the enemy leadership as seen through the fog (confidence-rated estimates and observed moves) and the Doctrine Book. Your council runs in advisory mode: adopt its recommendations one at a time, or delegate command entirely and watch it govern.
WAR v60 Jul 2026
Fidelity & Command Detail — validated against real wars
Real wars were run through the model. Eight conflicts — Korea, Vietnam, the Gulf War, Soviet–Afghanistan, WWII, the Falklands, Iraq and Russia–Ukraine — were driven through the simulation to see how its outcomes align with history. The model matched the historical ending type in most: decisive battlefield victories (Gulf, Falklands), negotiated stalemates (Korea, Ukraine), a superpower’s negotiated withdrawal (Afghanistan), coalition/economic collapse (WWII), and a home-front crisis despite battlefield dominance (Vietnam).
Home-front resilience (a fidelity fix the tests surfaced). The validation exposed that the losing side’s home front collapsed too readily, so stalemate wars wrongly ended in collapse. Real regimes differ: casualty-sensitive democracies crack (Vietnam) while authoritarian states endure years of an unpopular war. Home support now has a resilience floor tied to regime type and leadership resolve — so determined regimes are held in deep crisis but rarely fall to the war itself, and stalemates resolve by negotiation instead. This alone realigned Korea, Ukraine and Afghanistan with history.
📜 Historical Scenarios tab. Load a real war’s strategic conditions with one tap and watch the model play it out — each briefing carries the historical outcome and how the simulation aligned with it, plus a live read of what the current war is trending toward.
Enhanced war screen. A strategic summary bar now rides the top of the map — war-day, war scale, aims, DEFCON, who holds the initiative, and cumulative casualties (KIA) by side — and the decisive ground (corridors and each side’s main effort) is ringed as an OBJECTIVE.
More detail per system. Cumulative casualty accounting per side, a war-day clock tied to the strategic time-compression, and clearer trend reporting throughout.
WAR v59 Jul 2026
International Institutions & Political Economy
Blocs became bodies — a UN-like World Forum. The committed nations now vote collective resolutions — condemnation & sanctions against an atrocity side, a stabilization mandate when order collapses, an aid package for a losing ally, a ceasefire call when the world tires — and the great powers wield a veto. A collective sanctions regime bites far harder than nations acting one at a time.
A trade graph over the matrix. An economic web now lies across the relationship matrix, so sanctions, blockade and depression propagate along trade edges rather than as a flat number: a belligerent whose partners turn against it, or a world torn by a depression, watches its economy drag through the whole network. The GEO tab shows live trade disruption and each side's trade access.
Interveners now have their own aims. When a nation enters, it enters for something — a buffer zone, a land-grab, resource access, regime change, or simply to bleed both sides. A land-grab or regime backer hardens its side's aims and blocks a soft peace; a buffer or resource partner pushes for a settlement once ahead; a proxy commits little and walks away when its aim slips out of reach — taking its reserves with it.
A Peace Congress. When the system tires enough, the forum convenes a congress and puts terms — shaped by the battlefield and by the interveners — to both belligerents. Accept and the war ends by settlement; refuse and the holdout pays in coalition and world standing while the war grinds on. You weigh the terms from the 🌐 GEO tab.
Fixes. The bottom tab bar now scrolls horizontally so every tab stays readable on a phone; the World Forum no longer fixates on a single vetoed motion and now surfaces the full range of resolutions.
WAR v58 Jul 2026
The Nations Matrix — a war inside a standing world
The war is now fought inside an interconnected system of ~24 pre-existing nations. Each has real geopolitical power, a bloc, and a web of ties to every other nation. A new 🌐 GEO tab shows the whole board: who is at war, who is committed, who is on the fence, the sanctions pressure on each side, active interventions, and each principal's closest friends and frostiest rivals.
World impact is now proportional to the duration × scale of the war. A cumulative accumulator grows with time and with your war scale (limited → total), and it drags world order and both economies down in proportion. A brief limited war barely dents the world; a long total war reshapes it.
Geopolitical pressure propagates through the matrix. As the war grinds on, neutrals are pushed off the fence — first to sanction and back a side, then, for the major powers, to enter the war outright (a real reserve injection). When a nation enters, the ripple runs through its relationships: its allies are pulled in behind it, its rivals are pushed toward the other pole. A decisive front makes the undecided bandwagon toward the winner; a losing ally draws its friends in to the rescue.
Atrocities have a systemic price (tribunal ceiling). If a side crosses the line — sustained area-bombing, nuclear use — the international system turns on it: backers peel away as it becomes a pariah, and its coalition takes a cliff.
Black swans now cascade through the world. An outlier's severity scales with how stressed and how far along the war already is; each shock primes a different domain (raising the next swan's severity, not its frequency) and jolts the nations matrix — an economic swan sets off a sanctions cascade, a radical one convulses the order.
Map: the strategic picture goes deeper. A pulsing MUTUAL ASSURED DESTRUCTION arc links the two capitals at DEFCON ≤ 2, cut MSRs are marked INTERDICTED, and the enemy rear is fogged — their supply convoys read as drifting estimates, yours stay crisp.
An historian's verdict. When the war ends, the world writes it up: how it was won, how the nations finally aligned, who was drawn in, how far world order fell, and what kind of international system emerges from the wreckage.
WAR v57 Jul 2026
Theater Picture & Strategic Command
The war map now reads like a war map. A real front line (FLOT) is drawn across the theater, bending sector by sector with control, with BLUE and RED territory shaded to either side of it. You can see at a glance who holds what.
Troop movements, supply, and combat are shown. Animated movement arrows run from each side's rear toward the sectors it is reinforcing (the main effort gets a bold arrow); supply convoys flow as moving dots along every MSR, thinning and reddening when a line is cut; and active combat is marked with a pulsing crossed-swords glyph and an intensity ring on every contested sector.
A world-state HUD and a legend sit in the corners of the map — DEFCON, global tension, escalation, world order and both home fronts at a glance, plus a key to every symbol. All overlays toggle on and off.
New ⚔ THEATER tab — a command dashboard on the bottom deck: overlay switches, a full sector table (control · momentum · forces by arm · supply), MSR logistics with integrity and what each route feeds, quick main-effort assignment, and live theater-reserve readouts.
Deepened nuclear system & DEFCON interventions. Choose a nuclear posture — No First Use (cools the ladder, high crisis stability), Flexible Response, or Launch on Warning (maximum deterrence, but accidents at DEFCON 1 become far more likely). New strike options: a tactical strike that scours a single sector and invites reprisal, a demonstration that signals resolve and rattles the enemy without direct damage, and the existing strategic countervalue option. And real crisis management: open a hotline to talk the ladder down, stand down your alert, or field missile defence.
WORLD tab — Strategic Command Console — the escalation ladder as a live visual showing what each DEFCON rung unlocks, all the nuclear posture/strike/intervention controls in context, and a war-termination forecast (initiative, a war-weariness clock, and the most likely ending on current trajectories).
WAR v56 Jul 2026
Two-Process Event Architecture — the world runs on two clocks
A baseline system calibrated to the last century. The ordinary texture of war and geopolitics — command reliefs, recessions, mutinies, coups, sanctions, new belligerents, atrocity revelations, mediation offers, leadership changes — now fires from a time-inhomogeneous Poisson process whose per-class hazard rates are set to ~last-century base rates (a strategic time-compression of ~3 days per second). Its long-run frequency matches history: roughly one baseline event every ~18 s, ~6–7 per sim-year. This is the expectable, in-distribution world.
A separate black-swan engine for the outliers. True outliers come from their own slow, memoryless generator that deliberately does not sample from historical frequency — because the value of an outlier is its difference from the system. It fires roughly once per major war, the domain is drawn uniformly, and the specific event is procedurally composed so it is combinatorially novel and rarely repeats. Its effect is structural and persistent — it changes the rules of the world for a time, not just a number.
Five outlier domains, each with a recognisable archetype — Technology (e.g. an AGI fused into command; quantum decryption; autonomous swarms), Biology (e.g. a pandemic that drags every combatant regardless of the front), Human (a singular figure — industrialist, demagogue, peacemaker, defector, whistleblower — bound to a side or neutral), Economic (a systemic rupture on the scale of the Depression that resets the economic baseline for everyone), and Radicals (a 9/11-class asymmetric shock that spawns a persistent non-state threat striking rear areas regardless of the front, and can force a war-aims pivot).
Persistent "world forces." Each black swan installs an active modifier that keeps reshaping the war until it runs its course — a command-AI edge, a global pandemic drain, a courted figure, a world depression, a lingering insurgency. The WORLD tab now shows every Active World Force with its remaining time and effect.
You can respond to the world. New national-response levers appear when relevant: contain an outbreak, stand up a counter-terror campaign, or court an unaligned figure — each with a real cost and an uncertain result.
Deeper WORLD tab & visuals — a headline Global Tension index and a living era descriptor, a five-domain Instability Monitor (a barometer, not a prediction — black swans are unforecastable by design), the Active World Forces panel, a dedicated Black-Swan Chronicle, and threshold tick-marks drawn on every gauge.
WAR v55 Jul 2026
The World — strategic context
A war now sits inside a real world. A new 🌍 WORLD tab on the bottom deck models the political-economic-diplomatic system the war is fought inside. Nine dynamic gauges — each a function of real-world logic, each with named thresholds that change how the war can be fought — turn strategic actions into consequences that relate to something rather than a bare number.
DEFCON ladder (5→1) — derived from the escalation ladder and floored by each side's declared readiness. DEFCON 2 unlocks nuclear release; DEFCON 1 risks a catastrophic exchange. Modelled on the real US defence-readiness system.
Home-front support — domestic will, following the Mueller casualty-sensitivity and Gelpi/Feaver "rightness × winnability" models: it erodes with duration, casualties and economic pain, holds when you are visibly winning, and erodes faster when ambitious aims stall. Below 25% is a political crisis (forced de-escalation); below 12% the government falls and you lose the war without losing the front.
Economic stability — the sustainability of the war economy. Total war trades near-term output for long-term ruin; enemy counterforce/countervalue bombing and sanctions grind it; a limited war can even grow it. Collapse is a defeat path on its own, and it couples into the v54 war-economy that feeds mobilisation.
World-order stability, coalition cohesion & negotiation viability — the system's tolerance (escalation, atrocities and total war degrade it; low order invites sanctions and third-party intervention), whether your allies stay in (legitimacy + order − escalation − your own atrocities; a partner can defect and take their strength with them), and the rationalist off-ramp (Fearon war-termination): when both capitals are exhausted enough, a negotiated settlement becomes available.
War scale & war aims are yours to set — declare Limited / General / Total war and choose aims from Punitive → Limited → Coercion → Regime Change → Annihilation. Aims set the actual hold-to-win threshold on the front and how fast support decays; annihilation forbids any negotiated peace. Command efficacy — derived from the deep commander cognitive model (experience, adaptability, stress, fatigue) and C2 — lightly stiffens cohesion and sharpens operations on your main effort.
A causal ledger — the WORLD tab keeps a running record of how and what moved every value: every lever, event and threshold crossing is timestamped with its cause, so nothing changes without a reason you can read.
Outlier events can upend any of it — intelligence windfalls, propaganda victories, exposed atrocities, economic shocks, command friction, frontline mutinies and coups, third-party interventions, decapitations, mediation offers, diplomatic breakthroughs and nuclear near-misses fire at a rate that rises with world tension.
RED plays the whole board — the AI declares total war when losing, widens its aims when winning, matches your nuclear alert, and sues for peace when the war is no longer worth the cost.
WAR v54 Jul 2026
Instruments of National Power
A new ⚡ STRATEGIC tab in the War pane — a general commands more than divisions. Five theatre-level instruments now sit alongside Deep Command, each an intent lever that never touches a single unit (the chain of command, or the abstract model, executes): Special Forces direct action, deep reconnaissance, information / influence operations, military deception, and a strategic air campaign. Every one trades a real cost against a real effect, and the AI opponent wields the exact same toolkit against you.
Four new strategic resources tie it all together — Legitimacy (0–100%: your coalition standing and mobilisation base; countervalue force and failed covert ops burn it, restraint slowly heals it, and below 35% domestic war-weariness drags your morale). War economy (0–100%: what strategic bombing actually starves — it sets how fast your reserves regenerate to replace losses). National resolve (a hardened rally-round-the-flag bonus to cohesion — bombing an enemy's cities makes them fight harder, exactly as the historical record shows). And a shared Escalation ladder — countervalue actions by either side climb it; past 60% it unlocks total war: intensified attrition and countervalue for the enemy AI. These make "press bomb to win" a genuine dilemma rather than a free button.
Special Forces — direct action — a precise raid on any named enemy rear base (HQ, depot, airbase) without spending mass. Success rides on your commander's cunning; a hit on the HQ also disrupts enemy C2. A compromised raid loses the team and costs you legitimacy — SOF are a finite pool that regenerates slowly, so you can't spam them.
Special Forces — deep reconnaissance — insert a team to designate targets in a contested sector; better-directed fires shift that sector your way for a window. Cheaper and faster than a raid.
Information / influence operations (IO / PSYOP) — a non-kinetic campaign that degrades enemy morale and command cohesion (C2 jam). Cunning-gated — but it can be exposed, and blowback hardens enemy resolve and costs you legitimacy and morale.
Military deception (MILDEC) — a feint that fixes the enemy's reserves on a decoy sector, drawing their reinforcements away from your real main effort for a window. The single most force-multiplying lever when timed with an offensive.
Strategic air campaign — a sustained posture that burns reserve air every tick. Counterforce grinds the enemy's depots, airfields and war economy at low political cost. Countervalue / area attrites faster and shocks enemy morale, but bleeds your legitimacy, hardens enemy resolve, and climbs the escalation ladder. Enemy air defence attrites your campaign — suppress their airfield first (Strike Package / SOF raid) and your campaign lasts roughly three times as long. Air superiority is the enabler, exactly as in real doctrine.
The AI is a peer competitor now — a RED strategic director employs SOF, IO, deception and air campaigns on its own cadence, weighted by the RED commander's archetype: cunning commanders lean on information and deception, methodical ones on counterforce bombing, aggressive ones on countervalue and decapitation raids — and RED shows restraint too, standing a countervalue campaign down when its own legitimacy craters.
WAR v53 Jul 2026
Real Terrain, Deep Supply, Air Lifelines
Real-world theaters — a new Theater selector on the setup screen: Western Europe (Fulda Gap, Rhine Crossing, Ardennes Forest, Low Countries Corridor...), North African Desert (El Alamein, Tobruk, Kasserine Pass, Qattara Depression...), Eastern Front (Pripyat Marshes, Dnieper Line, Caucasus Passes, Volga Crossing...), Korean Peninsula (Chosin Reservoir, Pusan Perimeter, Imjin River...), plus the original Generic Front. Each theater assigns real sector names and matching terrain to all six sectors, with the two supply-corridor sectors deliberately picked as an actual historical chokepoint — a river crossing, a mountain pass, a depression that funnels all traffic through a gap — and labeled ⛛ CHOKEPOINT on both the setup screen and the front map.
Three new terrain types — Mountain Pass (⛰, the toughest grind — brutal, slow, attritional), Open Desert (░, the fastest — mobile, decisive fighting, matching the real North African campaigns), and Marshland (฿, second-toughest — swampy ground bogs everything down), alongside the existing six.
Supply is now a real, depleting resource — every sector tracks actual ammo and fuel stock (0-100), not just a derived percentage. Ammo burns fast in contact, slowly when idle; fuel burns from upkeep and faster under an aggressive posture. Both replenish from the MSR at a rate set by the same line-integrity math that already drove the old munitions multiplier — cut supply lines now visibly starve a sector over real time instead of just applying a permanent discount.
Running out of ammo now incapacitates a force, exactly like the real thing — below a critical ammo floor, a sector's force can no longer sustain the fight and measurably falls back in disorder: a fraction melts away into theater reserve every tick (re-equippable elsewhere), with 30% lost as stragglers and captured equipment during the pullback — worse still if fuel is also critical, since a force can't disengage cleanly without it. Verified in isolation: a sector forced to 4% ammo visibly loses strength, gains theater reserves, and fires a named "OUT OF AMMUNITION" event within seconds. Entering a rendered battle now also inherits the sector's real ammo/fuel stock as the starting depot levels, and battle consumption is folded back into the strategic stock when you leave — the two layers are now the same number, not two approximations of it.
Air power secures routes and can drop supplies from the sky — three ways air now matters strategically: (1) Air Escort — friendly air committed to a sector (via the existing Deploy lever) boosts that sector's own supply throughput, representing escorted convoys; (2) Air Interdiction — enemy air committed at a chokepoint sector now bombs the MSR running through it, degrading that line beyond whoever physically controls the chokepoint; (3) Resupply Drop — a new Air Command action that spends reserve transport sorties to airlift ammo and fuel directly into a sector's stock, completely bypassing a cut MSR — the only lifeline once a corridor is lost, deliberately less efficient than an open road but the difference between holding on and collapsing.
More detail on the front map — the selected theater's name and blurb now header the map; every active sector shows compact ammo/fuel gauges for both sides beneath its strength bar; chokepoint sectors carry a bold gold ⛛ label; a legend explains the symbols. The War tab's sector cards gained the same gauges.
WAR v52 Jul 2026
More Controls & UI Polish
War Options — three new pre-war dials on the setup screen: Front Scale (Small ×4 / Standard ×7 / Large ×10 — sets the theatre pool size), Victory Condition (hold 4, 5, or 6 of the six sectors to win outright), and a Reserve Ratio slider (10–40%, replacing the fixed ~14% held back). Untouched, all three default to exactly the v51 values — existing behaviour is bit-for-bit unchanged unless you touch a control.
Deployment Plan — set your starting formations — a new Auto/Manual toggle on the setup screen. Auto keeps the v51 intensity-weighted split. Manual hands you a row per sector: a weight stepper (how much of your force masses there) and a formation dropdown — Balanced, Armored Spearhead, Infantry Screen, Artillery Heavy, or Air Cavalry — that reshapes the unit-type mix sent to that sector (verified: an Armored Spearhead sector opens with roughly 2.5× the vehicle-to-infantry ratio of an untouched Balanced sector, drawn from the same theatre pool). RED continues to deploy automatically, so the choice is yours alone.
Air Command — deploy air assets — a new Deep Command lever: commit reserve air squadrons forward to a named active sector, or recall them back, on a short cooldown. Distinct from the automatic airbase-proximity bonus and from general reinforcement (which moves every unit type proportionally) — this is a targeted, on-demand air-power lever, available to both sides.
War tab reorganized into sub-views — FRONT / DEEP COMMAND / LOG pill navigation replaces one long scroll once a war is active, so each screen fits a phone without hunting through sector cards to find the controls. The Deep Command view now groups Main Effort, Posture, Air Command, Strike Package, and Sabotage under clear section headers; reserves now show air squadrons on hand alongside total power.
WAR v51 Jul 2026
Theatre Command — Playability
Theatre Command mode — a second command mode alongside Dual Command, chosen before pressing ⚔ BEGIN WAR. In Theatre Command you never handle a single unit's actions: entering a sector becomes OBSERVE, not control — both sides are already fully played by their commander's cognitive AI (that's how the engine has always worked), so watching one is watching the chain of command do its job, not you doing it. The order-issuing and battle-plan-drawing tools that let you hand-hold one fight go inert while observing (a message explains why); camera, pan and zoom stay live. As the flavor text puts it: a theatre commander is never in charge of the individual actions of his troops — that's what the chain of command is for.
AI-informed abstract resolution — every unrendered sector's fast-forward math now pulls from the real systems instead of a flat power ratio: the same per-unit-type damage-matchup table fireAt() uses (so an infantry-heavy force actually loses faster to an armor-heavy one of equal "power" — verified: two forces of identical flat power, one all-infantry one all-armor, and the armor force won convincingly both directions of the matchup), the acting commander's full trait profile (aggression, cunning, tempo, resolve, logistics — not just experience), each sector's terrain (six flavors: open/urban/hills/river/forest/coastal, each damping or sustaining the grind), and a theatre-wide cohesion term. Same brains driving every sector — Patton and Zhukov still fight like Patton and Zhukov in an unrendered sector — just resolved analytically instead of frame-by-frame.
Deep Command panel — four theatre-level levers, none of them touching a single unit: Main Effort (redirect reserve reinforcement flow to a chosen sector instead of the default weakest-sector heuristic), Theatre Posture (aggressive/balanced/defensive — reshapes your whole force's fast-forwarded combat math and counterattack tempo), Strike Package (spend reserve power to damage a named enemy rear base directly from the War tab, on a cooldown), and Sabotage Operation (a cyber/space-flavored jab at the enemy Force HQ or a supply corridor's throughput, success rolled against commander cunning, on a cooldown).
New consequences — theatre morale (win/loss streaks shift a −1..1 modifier theatre-wide, decaying back to neutral, felt through the resolution formula); a global C2 modifier tied to your own Force HQ's integrity, independent of any single sector's proximity — lose your HQ and every sector feels it, not just the nearby ones; and wrecked bases — a depot, airbase, or HQ that's driven to zero integrity (via a Strike Package, for instance) is permanently degraded, distinct from the existing temporary 35%-floor overrun dip, and won't fully recover for the rest of the war.
Overview enhancements — momentum arrows (▲/▼) on every active sector, both on the front map and in the War tab list, show which way each abstract fight is trending without opening it; a persistent Theatre Status strip reports both sides' global C2, morale, and posture at a glance; rear bases now list their integrity (and WRECKED state) directly in the War tab.
Renamed to WAR — this is the final shape of the file for this design era; title and header updated accordingly.
Theater v50 Jul 2026
WAR — Final Release of the Current Paradigm
Simulation of war, not independent battles — a single massive theater front replaces the one-off engagement. Your OOB selection ×7 per side is distributed across six battle sectors plus a theater reserve. Battles exist as nodes at fixed coordinates on the strategic map and are only physically rendered while you command them: click any node to spin up the full tactical engine there (terrain built from the node's seed, forces spawned from its current operational strength). Every other active sector resolves in parallel on the same war clock through an operational model (Lanchester attrition × commander quality × supply throughput). Tab between battles freely — survivors are counted back into the node when you leave, and the fight carries on at operational tempo. Classic single skirmishes (▶ Engage) remain fully available when no war is running.
Battlefields interact through the supply network — each side runs two MSRs from rear depot bases to the front. Two corridor sectors sit astride the main supply routes: losing control of your corridor collapses that line's integrity, and every battle fed by it fights at reduced munitions — depot stock and starting/ongoing ammunition are hard-capped by line throughput in the rendered battle, attrition output is scaled in abstract ones, C4ISR convoys fail to get through, and reinforcement flow from reserve slows. Airbase in range → +2 sorties committed to the rendered battle. Force HQ in range → hardened C2 integrity and cyber defense. Bases near an enemy-held sector can be overrun, degrading their lines.
Persistent operational war — losses persist between battles; beaten forces retreat 55% of their remainder to theater reserve; reserves automatically reinforce the weakest sector along (and only along) functioning MSRs; frozen fronts see-saw through counterattacks until one side holds five sectors, a side's total power collapses, or a fully decided front settles on current lines. Front map shows live control rings, strength bars, munitions throughput, MSR integrity, and pulses the sector under your command.
Historical theater commanders — the staff AI for each nation is statted from a documented historical commander of that country (all deceased historical figures: Patton, Montgomery, Guderian, Foch, Dayan, Zhukov, Peng Dehuai, Putnik, Monash, Currie, Maceo, Bolívar and more — 24 profiles), with traits derived from their recorded command style. The full v43/v47 cognitive machinery — trait jitter, stress/fatigue, confirmation and optimism bias, memories, opponent modelling, softmax decision loop, learning — is retained on top, so the profiles bias behaviour without making it deterministic.
UI — new War tab (front dashboard: sector cards with take-command buttons, MSR status, reserves, war log) and a ⚔ FRONT/BATTLE header toggle; the front map itself is clickable. The Engage button routes into the war while one is running; Reset stands the theater down.
Ship Hardening (v50 security pass)
Content-Security-Policy — the file now declares default-src 'none' with no connect/img/object/frame sources: fully self-contained, no network access, no remote code, no exfiltration surface. Referrer disabled.
Last-resort error trap — a top-level window.onerror handler routes any uncaught error into the debug overlay instead of white-screening; all v49/v50 subsystems remain individually guarded and degrade gracefully.
Data integrity — the historical-general table is frozen (Object.freeze); all dynamic text rendered into the War pane is HTML-escaped.
Theater v49 Jul 2026
Consolidation Release — last of the current paradigm
Visible projectiles on the map — every round in flight now renders on the 2D COP as a moving head with a directional trail, differentiated by class: bullets streak, shells loft and burst, missiles glow with exhaust, ATGMs trail a command wire back to the launcher, AA missiles weave, rockets puff, bombs tumble, torpedoes wake, ballistic warheads glow on terminal descent. Projectile lifetimes lengthened so flight paths are readable; impact flashes on terminal hits. (Fixes the previous static, non-fading tac-map fire lines.)
Bottom tab deck (v11 paradigm restored) — the tab strip returns to the bottom bar as in v11, now spanning the full window above the feed: Live · Command · AAR · Intel · Tactics · Wiki · Notes (+ the injected C4ISR tab). Panes open as a drawer sliding up from the bottom; clicking the active tab closes it. The map now gets the full width previously taken by the right panel. Patch Notes became the Notes tab.
Live tab restored — the v11 Live readout (engagement clock, force strength, fires & effect, kills by arm, losses, morale) is back and wired into the loop. It had been dead code since the pane was dropped from the HTML.
C2 link model — think free, act under command — every unit is ON or OFF the command net: HQ radio range (COMMS-satellite modulated) plus tactical relays through linked friendlies, degraded by EW jamming and cyber intrusion. Linked units hold formation slots, receive side orders and route support requests up the chain. Units cut from the net receive no orders, drop formation discipline, and fight on their own initiative — at an accuracy and morale price that grows with isolation. Severed links draw red-dashed on the C2 overlay with a ✕ marker on the unit.
Deep combined-arms engine — live typed synergies scanned continuously: infantry screens spoil AT shots against accompanied armor (−25%); armor steadies nearby infantry (accuracy up, suppression sheds faster); AD umbrellas degrade enemy air accuracy over covered troops; artillery with a linked forward observer at the target shoots tighter (+10%); JTAC-designated air strikes gain accuracy and damage. Each formation group earns a Combined-Arms score (arms mix + fires on call + AD cover + net connectivity) feeding a team accuracy bonus and cohesion regeneration — shown on the Command pane.
Support request net — linked units in contact generate FIRE MISSION, CAS and emergency RESUPPLY requests routed up the chain with latency driven by HQ integrity and cyber state; approvals task real artillery tubes and strike aircraft onto the requested target (honoured by the targeting system), or push depot stock to starving units. Denials happen when no asset is free or depots are dry. Full request feed on the Command pane.
Cyber & space domain — per-side RECON / COMMS / GPS constellations and cyber offense/defense ratings derived from national quality. Recon-satellite passes sweep the map on a cadence and dump contacts into the intel picture (visible as a scanning band); COMMS health stretches or shrinks the C2 net; GPS health biases guided-munition accuracy. Cyber operations fire offense-vs-defense on a cadence: C2 intrusion, ISR spoofing (contact wipes + phantom tracks drawn as amber ?), logistics attack (frozen convoys), AD suppression, GPS/SATCOM jamming. Constellations self-heal; blocked intrusions harden the defender. All state on the Command pane.
Command tab — new pane uniting the chain of command: net status per side, the resurrected C2 command-chain panel (HQ integrity, strikes, restores), Deep Strike operations, the support request feed, combined-arms scores, and the cyber/space picture.
Bug Fixes
Dead #live pane — renderLive() had silently no-op'd since the Live pane was removed from the HTML. Pane restored; the duplicate #adaptPanel/#ordersPanel skeleton it injected (colliding with the Tactics pane IDs) removed.
