Dead #c2Panel reference — renderC2Panel() and renderDeepStrikePanel() wrote to an element that didn't exist; both are now live on the Command pane. renderDeepStrikePanel() also appended (innerHTML+=) into the C2 panel, which would have grown without bound had the element existed — it now renders into its own container.
Tac-map tracer alpha bug — the old fire-line alpha used the constant t.life/0.3 instead of remaining life, so lines never faded and showed no flight progress. Replaced by the animated projectile renderer.
Header versioning — the header still read "THEATER v47" while the title said v48; both now agree.
Theater v48 Jun 2026
C4ISR Upgrade Layer (v48)
Formation hierarchy — Corps → Brigade → Battalion → Company — a real echelon tree is built each battle on top of the existing C2 chain and formation groups. Brigades map to the three division HQs; companies map to the live platoon/company groups; leaf companies own the actual units. Orders propagate downward with per-echelon delay that stretches when the parent brigade's C2 HQ integrity is degraded or the echelon's coherence is low. Coherence is computed live from unit spread vs each echelon's frontage. Company-level orders drive the existing group posture (edge-triggered) so the proven low-level steering still executes — the hierarchy issues intent, the local commander adapts.
Corps intent → differentiated brigade orders — each corps reads the side's real commander risk tolerance, force ratio, and PLAN main axis, then assigns the main-effort brigade ATTACK while others DEFEND / RESERVE / RETROGRADE. Intent is re-evaluated periodically and re-propagated through the chain.
ISR / sensor network — every unit yields typed sensors (VISUAL / UAV / RADAR / SIGINT) with class-appropriate range and accuracy. A per-side IntelPicture tracks contacts with a confidence that decays with age, fed from the existing per-side detection ground-truth and refined by terrain LOS, weather, EW masking and target stealth. Confident contacts sharpen the legacy last-known-position fog markers.
Physical logistics network — supply nodes are built from real depots + airbases (+ neutral factories). Supply convoys physically run rear-hub → depot, refilling the real depot stock the truck economy already draws on, and can be interdicted by enemy aircraft in range or ground units astride the route. Each unit's MSR is traced to its nearest node and rated CONNECTED / STRAINED / CUT by throughput (roads boost, enemies / rivers / severe terrain degrade). Genuinely cut units bleed ammo, fuel and morale.
New "C4ISR" panel + 3 map overlays — the right-panel C4ISR tab shows the live echelon tree (order, coherence, strength per node), the ISR summary (contacts tracked, average confidence, sensor mix), and the logistics state (depot levels, convoys en route, connected / strained / cut counts) for both sides. Three new map-overlay toggles: ⬢ Echelons (chain lines + order/coherence markers), ◇ Intel Picture (confidence-graded contact diamonds), ⛟ Logistics (nodes, convoys, MSRs, cut markers).
Layered, never destructive — the whole C4ISR layer is rebuilt each engagement and fully guarded; if any subsystem throws, the legacy command / intel / logistics systems continue unchanged and the sim never freezes. The new layer takes precedence while it is running but degrades gracefully to the v47 behaviour.
Commander AI Framework
Full cognitive AI decision loop — every commander now runs a five-stage decision cycle every 5–18 seconds (faster for high-tempo commanders, slower under stress): Analyse battlefield → Generate plans → Score via staff analysis + personality filter → Predict enemy + counter-risk → Softmax selection → Execute → Learn.
Battlefield analysis — the AI reads live game state each cycle: force ratio, supply level, morale, territory control, enemy artillery presence, open flanks, and terrain suitability per plan type. This feeds the staff scoring.
Staff analysis + personality filter — plans are scored by objective analysis (force ratio, supply, morale, enemy strength, terrain) and then adjusted by personality (aggression scales offensive plans, risk tolerance scales risky ones, logistics commanders prefer artillery prep and pauses). Hard staff overrides block suicidal choices — a frontal assault against overwhelming odds is penalised by −40 regardless of personality. Verified: blocked in 98% of cases when outnumbered.
Enemy prediction + counter-risk — each commander maintains an opponent model updated by observing enemy behaviour (flanking frequency, artillery activity, retreats). A plan that would be countered by a likely enemy response incurs a counter-risk penalty, so commanders naturally avoid walking into traps they've observed before.
Softmax selection — plans are chosen probabilistically (not always the best one). Temperature is controlled by creativity and stubbornness: creative commanders explore more, stubborn ones are more decisive. Verified: a creative commander picks all 5 plan types across 300 decisions — choices feel human, not robotic.
Cognitive State: Personality + Emotion + Learning
New personality traits — commanders now have adaptability, stubbornness, creativity, preparation, and risk tolerance in addition to the existing deep traits — all rolled at battle start with jitter per archetype.
Emotional state — confidence, stress, and fatigue are dynamic fields that change during battle. A string of failed assaults raises stress and drops confidence, which then penalises offensive plan scores. High fatigue pushes toward operational pauses. These shift the AI's choices mid-battle without hard-coding transitions.
Learning system — outcomes shift memory values (breakthrough, flank, artillery, defense) that in turn weight future plan preferences. A commander who got a breakthrough succeeds at frontal assault more readily; one who keeps getting flanked starts screening those threats. Objective captures and losses fire learning events in real time.
Execution & Integration
Routes into existing systems — the AI plan is executed by mapping onto the existing doctrine (FRONTAL_ASSAULT→blitzkrieg/mass, FLANK_ATTACK→maneuver, ARTILLERY_PREP→precision, DEFENSE_IN_DEPTH→defense) and the formation plan system. It announces plan transitions on the ticker with commander name and emotional state.
AAR shows final cognitive state — the after-action report now displays each commander's confidence, stress, fatigue, and last plan type at battle end.
Theater v46 Jun 2026
Formation Groups & Cohesion
Formations are real groups, not just spawn positions — units are task-organized into platoon/company-sized groups (≤8 units, by HQ sector). Each group has a designated leader unit, slot assignments (positions within the formation relative to the group centroid), a cohesion score (0-100), and a posture FSM (advance/hold/withdraw/assault).
Slot-based cohesion steering — each unit gets a gentle background pull toward its assigned formation slot, keeping the group together without overriding individual combat. Infantry flows behind armour. The force is stronger when the unit is far from its slot and nearly zero when fighting — so units have real battlefield autonomy while still belonging to a coordinated element.
Cohesion matters — a spread group loses cohesion, which bleeds morale and adds an accuracy penalty. Well-maintained groups fight better. Cohesion is visualized as a dashed ring on the tac map when the group is scattered.
Frontline Visualization
Live contested boundary — a gold dashed glow is traced between the two forces each tick, showing where the frontline lies. Updates dynamically as forces advance and withdraw.
Key Terrain — Rivers, Bridges, Cities, Airbases
Rivers (0-2 per map) run N-S with random bends and block ground movement — units deflect along them rather than crossing. Airbases, bridges, cities, and factories are procedurally placed each battle.
Bridges are destructible chokepoints with HP bars — the only crossing points on a river. Each bridge is also a tactical objective that both sides contest. Bridges link to the road network.
Cities (named: FALLENHAVEN, BRIDGEMONT, KESSLER, VOLKOV…) are destructible strategic objectives. Fire accumulates structural damage, degrading cover and eventually partially ruining buildings. Cities with large populations are minor objectives on the map.
Airbases (one per side, deep rear) repair nearby friendly aircraft when intact. If the airbase is destroyed or captured, aircraft lose their repair facility. Shown with runway glyph.
Factories near supply depots boost ammo/fuel regeneration rates — a reason to defend the industrial rear. All new structures show HP bars when damaged.
Road Network & Deep Logistics
Road network — a procedural road grid (MSR West/East + supply spurs) connects airbases, depots, and objectives. Units on roads move +45% faster. Supply trucks automatically exploit roads to reach the front.
Factory supply bonus — factories near depots increase resupply trickle rate. Factories near roads get an additional throughput bonus. A reason to fight for the industrial center.
Depot vulnerability — enemy artillery in range can interdict enemy supply depots, degrading ammo and fuel. Deep fires now have a concrete logistics effect.
Forward Supply Posts (FSP) — a supply truck that is stationary for 10+ seconds with cargo becomes a temporary forward post with an extended 3.5× resupply radius, letting it sustain a forward line without returning to depot.
Airbase aircraft repair — aircraft near their side's airbase slowly repair hull points when the base is intact.
City damage accumulation — sustained combat near a city gradually destroys it: cover bonus degrades, buildings crumble, fire indicators appear.
Realistic Command Delay
Per-echelon command delay — orders travel Force HQ → Division HQ → Unit through three separate delay layers. Force→Division delay scales with commander tempo; Division→Unit delay scales with HQ integrity and field-commander initiative. Each unit gets ±20% noise to simulate radio fog. A high-tempo commander with intact C2 propagates orders in under a second; a disrupted HQ with a by-the-book field commander can take 6-8s.
Theater v45 Jun 2026
Deep Reconnaissance & Fog of War
Per-side detection — spotting is now tracked independently for each side (spottedBy.BLUE/RED) with a short contact memory, instead of one global "spotted" flag. What BLUE sees and what RED sees are now genuinely separate.
Recon assets & the recce screen — drones (×1.6), EW/SIGINT (×1.4), special forces and scouts (×1.5), aircraft (×1.25) and recon vehicles detect better and further, and their contacts light up the enemy for the whole force. Lose your recon screen and you fight half-blind.
Detection-gated targeting — a unit can only engage enemies its side has detected (point-blank and air contacts excepted). Recon now has real teeth: undetected enemies can't be fired on, so seeing first is a decisive edge. Verified not to reintroduce freezing — unseen-enemy units advance to contact instead of stalling.
Fog-of-war visualization — new "🌫 Fog" map toggle (Off / BLUE / RED). Undetected enemy units are hidden; their last known position is shown as a fading dashed "?" ghost that ages out over ~25s. Recon assets show a sensor-arc marker.
Hitboxes & Formations
Physical unit footprints — every ground unit has a collision radius by type (armour 2.6, infantry 1.9, etc.). A spatial-grid resolution pass pushes overlapping friendly units apart so they physically cannot stack into a blob — a hard floor under the soft separation steering. Infantry flows around armour (lighter units yield). Verified: 15 stacked units spread to proper spacing across a 21-unit frontage.
Suppression — Deepened & Freeze-Checked
Removed redundant instant-pins — two hidden code paths (direct hits and arty splash) were setting pinned=true on every hit, bypassing the push-through / momentum / mass-assault resistance and re-pinning units every tick. Pinning is now decided in exactly one place (the hysteresis logic), closing a hidden contributor to freezing.
Suppression realism pass — suppression now primarily degrades return fire: accuracy falls with intensity (not just when pinned) and rate of fire drops while suppressed. Near-misses suppress (incoming fire is suppressive whether or not it hits). Cover matters — troops in forest/urban/structures resist suppression, hold their nerve, and recover faster. Veterans and high-resolve commanders shake it off quicker.
Tactical Realism
Flanking & armour facing — armoured vehicles have thick frontal and thin side/rear armour. Hitting a vehicle from its flank (+1 effective penetration) or rear (+2, plus bonus damage) can defeat armour that would bounce off the front. Units now face their direction of movement so this is positional.
Flanking maneuver AI — cunning commanders and maneuver/recon elements curl their approach to take enemy-held objectives from the flank rather than charging straight in, while main-effort armour fixes the front. Rewards the new flank-armour mechanic with real maneuver.
No-stall respects defence — the anti-freeze backstop now leaves defensive/Fabian doctrines holding owned ground static (long fuse, only moves if their sector is genuinely threatened) and exempts units recovering in the withdraw/rally states, so deliberate defensive play isn't shoved forward.
Stability & Redundancy
Subsystem isolation — all ~22 per-tick systems now run inside an individual safeStep guard. If any one throws, the error is logged once and the rest still run — the sim degrades gracefully instead of freezing because a single subsystem hit a bad state. No more "one line of code stops everything."
Diagnostic upgraded — the press-d freeze monitor now also reports recon-asset count, how much of the force is visible to the enemy, and the current fog view.
Theater v44 Jun 2026
The Real Freeze Bug — Detection Gate
Found the root cause of mass freezing — units that had acquired a target they couldn't yet see (fog of war / distance) hit a "detection fire gate" that made them face the contact and continue — skipping ALL movement. At battle start, before detection resolves, this froze entire formations in place facing the enemy. Every other movement system (objective pull, assault override) lived after this gate, so none of it ran.
Movement is no longer gated by detection — only firing is — a unit that can't see its target now advances toward its objective (or the last-known/expected enemy position) to gain observation, with separation so it doesn't stack. Forces move to contact instead of freezing on the line of departure.
No-Stall Guarantee
Hard backstop against frozen formations — every ground unit now tracks how long it has been effectively stationary. If it stalls more than ~2.5s while the battle is live and it doesn't firmly hold its objective, a forward urge ramps up (toward the nearest contestable objective, or the enemy if all are held) until it moves. A real force is never idle mid-battle — but units legitimately holding a won objective still hold.
Freeze Diagnostic Overlay
Built-in state monitor — press d (or quadruple-tap) to toggle a live diagnostic showing, per tick: how many ground units are moving vs stalled (and the longest stall), how many are pinned / suppressed / assaulting / routing, and the top behaviour states. The panel border turns red if more than half the force is stalled, so freezing is now visible at a glance.
Carries forward v43.2 — the assault override (assaulting units push through "hold and fire"), movement inertia (momentum resists reversal), and pin hysteresis (pins evaluated on a timer, not a per-tick coin flip) all remain in place beneath these fixes.
Theater v43.2 Jun 2026
Freezing Fix (assault marker but frozen)
Assault override — the real bug: the doctrine FSM frequently sets movement to zero ("hold and fire" at standoff range), and the assault flag only affected suppression/pin math — it never actually forced movement. So units showed the assault marker (▲) while standing still. Assaulting units now push forward toward their objective/enemy regardless of what the doctrine FSM wants — they never stall to zero while assaulting.
Movement inertia — momentum is now physical: it's harder to stop a moving column and reverse than to keep pushing. The new heading blends with the previous one (weighted by built-up momentum), and attempts to reverse a charge are strongly damped. Units that are moving tend to keep moving forward instead of stuttering to a halt every time the doctrine flickers to "hold".
Pin hysteresis — the pin check was a per-tick coin flip, so a unit with 50% pin resistance was actually pinned ~half of every second (reading as "frozen"). Pins are now evaluated on a ~1.2s timer with hysteresis, the suppression-intensity threshold to pin was raised, and an assaulting unit with any momentum breaks the pin outright.
Theater v43.1 Jun 2026
Clustering / Freezing Fix
Fixed the dense-blob clustering — units were piling into a tight knot on the objective flag within seconds, turning battles into one-sided massacres instead of dispersed fights on multiple fronts. Root causes: (1) the objective pull dragged every assigned unit onto the exact centre point; (2) separation steering was far too weak (4-unit radius, near-zero weight) and a second doctrine pass set mass-assault spacing to almost nothing.
Strong unified separation — replaced the two weak/conflicting separation passes with one system: a 5–9 unit spacing radius (doctrine-aware — mass concentrates, asymmetric disperses) with a falloff force that holds a real minimum gap. Boosted further when units are contesting an objective so the force fans out across its frontage instead of stacking on the flag. Verified: 14 units converging on one point now hold ~7-unit spacing across 35 units of frontage instead of a 4-unit blob.
Units disperse on the objective — the objective pull now stops at the capture-radius edge (not the centre), and the no-target advance applies separation inline, so units settle into a dispersed screen covering the objective rather than converging on a single dot.
Multi-front contact — with dispersed formations both forces advance to the middle and trade fire across the front (verified ~23 contact pairs in a 24-unit test) instead of one blob getting focus-fired and melting. Heated battles on multiple fronts, not a quick massacre.
Theater v43 Jun 2026
Critical Freeze Fix (v43b)
Fixed units freezing on owned objectives — diagnosed from gameplay: in asymmetric missions (e.g. Extraction) units were assigned to an objective their own side already held (the extraction point they spawn on), so they sat on it and froze in a cluster while the enemy advanced — turning a two-front battle into a massacre. Units now detect when their assigned objective is firmly held (>72% control) and instead push to the nearest contested or enemy-held objective, or advance on the enemy centroid if everything is held. The stop-deadzone was also tightened so units press all the way onto contested ground instead of halting short.
Applies in and out of contact — both the targetless approach-march movement and the in-combat objective pull now skip already-held objectives, so the whole force keeps advancing into the fight instead of camping ground it already owns. Verified: a unit that previously sat frozen now advances ~19 units toward contested ground within 3 seconds.
Deep Commander System
16 force-commander archetypes — expanded from 8 to 16: Reckless, Aggressive, Armored Fist, Shock Troops, Methodical, Set-Piece, Defensive, Fabian, Cautious, Attritionist, Maneuverist, Deep Battle, Infiltrator, Guardsman, Opportunist, and Logistician. Each has a named commander (rank + surname) and a richer trait set.
Deeper traits — commanders now have aggression, caution, armorBias, tempo plus cunning (flanks, smoke, enabling objectives, deception), resolve (resistance to morale collapse / willingness to push through), and logistics (attention to supply & counter-logistics). These feed planning, the assault decision, and targeting.
Field Commanders
Two command echelons — under the force commander, each division (HQ-A/B/C) now has its own field commander with one of 6 sector archetypes (Thruster, Steady, Cautious, Opportunist, Dogged, By-the-Book) and traits for initiative, aggression, caution, and resolve. Shown in the C2 panel.
Initiative matters — a high-initiative, high-resolve field commander holds his sector together even with comms to higher cut: reduced morale/accuracy penalties and units keep acting on the plan. A by-the-book commander with poor comms leaves units hesitant (full penalties).
Realistic Command & Control
Sector-based divisions — units are now assigned to the division holding their sector (HQ-A north, HQ-B center, HQ-C south) with soft load-balancing, instead of pure round-robin. Divisions hold contiguous frontage like real formations.
C2 assignment bug fixed — the C2 chain was being reset after forces were built, wiping every unit's division assignment (the C2 panel showed empty divisions). C2 now resets before force generation so assignments persist.
Decapitation & degradation — EW jamming and fires still degrade an HQ; a degraded HQ's effect on its units is now modulated by the field commander's ability to hold the sector together. Order-propagation delay, accuracy, morale, and coordination all flow through the C2 hierarchy.
Pinning & The Central Thrust
Pinning fixed for the main effort — main-effort units tasked to the vital/central objective now always press the assault, giving them up to 95% pin resistance in a mass assault. Verified: a central unit under fire advances ~100% of the time and only slows ~9% even when momentarily pinned.
Some forces always take the middle — the planner now places the vital/central objective first in the supporting-force rotation, so even when the main effort is committed elsewhere, a supporting element is always sent to contest the center. The middle is never left empty.
Broader will to assault — the assault decision now blends force-commander resolve and field-commander initiative, so determined commanders push through fire across more of the front, not just at one point.
Theater v42 Jun 2026
Anti-Paralysis — Push-Through Mechanics
Fixed formation paralysis — the compounding of suppression + pinning + frequent replanning + risk-avoidance + local force-ratio pressure froze whole formations. The fix keeps suppression meaningful but makes it overcomeable by a determined assault.
Assault / push-through posture — units can enter an ASSAULT state that pushes through fire and accepts casualties to keep the advance moving: suppression morale-drain is halved, pin resistance +50%, the effective rout threshold drops by 10 (they hold instead of breaking), and they take ~15% more damage as the cost of exposure. Marked with a yellow ▲ on the map.
Mass assault — when several units assault together near each other, the coordinated push gains pin resistance +50%, suppression recovery +25%, a +40% assault-continuation bias, and the commander commits the reserve at a lower threshold to press it home. A determined mass assault under fire now has up to 95% pin resistance — it breaks through rather than freezing.
Momentum multiplier — a moving column builds momentum (up to +35% speed and +40% pin resistance) so it keeps moving; momentum decays when stalled. Movement has inertia instead of stop-start hesitation.
Combat Posture FSM
Graceful degradation, not freeze/rout — every unit runs a combat FSM: Fight → Disengage → Withdraw (behind cover) → Rally → Counterattack → Fight. A suppressed, low-morale unit breaks contact and falls back to recover, then rallies and counterattacks — instead of freezing in place or routing off the field. Verified to cycle without deadlock.
Tuning
Central force preserved — the planner still weights the vital/central objective as the main effort, so the AI commits a solid central thrust despite casualties rather than treating the middle as too dangerous.
Slower command decisions — mid-battle replanning interval raised to 16–28s (was 6–14s); real command decisions on the fly take time, and the frantic micro-replanning was feeding the paralysis.
Even formations — light separation steering spreads units that get too close, so a column forms an even line/wedge instead of collapsing onto a single point.
Mass-assault narration — the ticker now reports a determined assault ("pressing a determined assault — pushing through fire, accepting losses to take the ground").
Theater v41 Jun 2026
Operational Battle Plans
Commanders draw up a plan before the battle — each commander analyzes the mission and objectives, then task-organizes the force into a main effort (the decisive thrust at the highest-value objective), supporting elements (secondary objectives, spread across them), and a reserve held back for mid-battle commitment. Every unit gets an assigned objective and role.
Coordinated maneuver — clustering fixed — the root cause of backline clustering was that every unit independently picked the single highest-value objective, so they all converged on one point. Now units follow their plan-assigned objective, so the force divides among objectives in a coordinated way. Verified: a 20-unit force now spreads across all available objectives instead of stacking on one.
Personality shapes the plan — aggressive commanders allocate a bigger main effort and small reserve; cautious commanders hold a larger reserve and screen more; armor-biased commanders weight tanks into the main effort. Main-effort units pull harder than supporting elements.
Mid-Battle Adaptation
Commanders adjust the plan live — every 6–14 seconds (faster for high-tempo commanders) they review: if a clearly better objective emerges they shift the main effort; if the main effort stalls or a breakthrough opens they commit the reserve; if an objective is firmly held they free those units to push onward. Each decision is announced on the ticker with its reasoning.
Deeper AI Reasoning — Enabling Objectives
Indirect paths to victory — the AI now reasons about objectives that don't win directly but make the win achievable. Cutting a supply waypoint (MSR/FUEL/DEPOT) chokes the enemy's whole effort; seizing observation/key terrain (OP/HILL/RIDGE) dominates the sector with fires; opening a corridor/breach enables maneuver. These get extra weight in planning even when they aren't the literal win condition. Verified: supply waypoints now out-rank plain flanks in the planner.
Enabling-target priority — experienced and maneuverist commanders recognize that killing enemy supply, EW, and fires degrades the whole enemy effort, and weight those targets harder in acquisition. Maneuverists actively hunt the enemy rear.
Plans surfaced everywhere — each commander's plan rationale ("secure MSR BRAVO to choke enemy supply, then take CITADEL") appears on the opening ticker, the FEED log, and the after-action report (including how many times the plan was adapted mid-battle).

Posture analysis — every 6 seconds the engine analyzes each side's centroid movement (toward/away from enemy), routing fraction, pinned fraction, force ratio, and which objective they're massing on, then classifies the broad action: advancing, flanking, massing, regrouping, fighting withdrawal, general retreat, holding, pinned, or dominant — flavored by the commander's archetype.

Commander Personalities

Rolled fresh each battle with small jitter so no two are identical.
Traits shape behavior — aggression scales how far and hard units push toward enemy objectives (reckless commanders reach 1.4× further and pull 1.6× harder); cautious commanders consolidate what they hold; armorBias makes armor lead; experience gives a small accuracy edge (±0.06) and faster morale recovery (well-led troops resist panic). The commander archetype also colors the movement narration.
Goal-Based Victory
Win by achieving the mission, not waiting out a timer — victory now comes from completing the mission's objective (capture the citadel, hold the airfield to T120, cut 3 of 4 MSR waypoints, get the element to the extraction point, etc.). The old "wait for the clock" path is gone; a composite-score check at T160 remains only as a hard backstop so a battle can't run forever.
Backline Clustering Fix
Units no longer freeze in the rear — the root cause: units with no acquired enemy target hit a continue and stopped, so rear-echelon and not-yet-engaged units clustered at the back. Now targetless units advance toward the most valuable contestable objective (scaled by commander aggression), so the whole force moves forward to take ground.
Theater v39 Jun 2026
Behavior Fix — Freeze & Retreat
Diagnosed the death spiral — units were freezing and routing before fighting. Cause: the v36-37 suppression + stagnation + harassment systems stacked. Units got suppressed before contact, the pin threshold (morale<55) froze healthy units, frozen units accumulated stagnation morale drain, which triggered harassment fire, which suppressed them more. Recovery (0.12/s) couldn't keep up with drains (up to 12+/s). Result: morale collapsed and units retreated without a fight.
Removed forced-movement penalties — the stagnation morale drain and the artillery harassment-fire-on-static-clusters mechanics are gone. Units are no longer punished for holding position. (The artillery smoke-screen AI is kept.)
Suppression no longer freezes units — pinned units now slow their advance to ~45% under fire (realistic bounding/rushing) instead of being completely frozen. The pin threshold dropped from morale<55 to morale<32, so only genuinely shaken units are pinned. Suppression also clears faster (2.5s vs 3.5s).
Morale rebalanced — base recovery raised 0.12→0.45/s, veteran recovery 0.6→0.9/s. Suppress drain 2.5→1.4/s, artillery suppression drain 8.0→4.0/s, isolation 0.8→0.4/s, death contagion 6→4. A supported unit under small-arms fire now recovers morale instead of draining; even worst-case drains are recoverable once fire lifts.
Defense units hold the line — they no longer constantly drift back to structures. Only routing or badly-suppressed units fall back to cover.
Objective / Territory Control
Capture points replace forced movement — every battle now seeds 5 objectives across the contested middle of the map (a vital CENTER plus four flanking points). Units advance because taking and holding ground is rewarded, not because standing still is punished.
Control mechanic — each objective has a 0-100 control value that shifts toward whichever side has more combat presence inside the 16-unit capture radius. At ≥75 it's Blue-held, ≤25 Red-held, with a neutral band between. Capturing the vital center is logged as a turning point.
Objective-seeking movement — units within 60 units of an objective are drawn to contest it, prioritizing neutral/enemy-held and actively contested points (and the vital center counts double). This gives a positive reason to move forward and take ground.
Holding ground boosts morale — units near an objective their side controls gain +0.5/s morale; contesting a neutral/enemy objective gives +0.18/s (the initiative of attacking). Taking ground now feels good and reinforces the advance.
Territory decides close battles — the timeout victory condition is now 65% combat power + 35% territory control, so out-fighting the enemy AND out-positioning them both matter. A territory bar in the HUD shows who holds the ground.
Map rendering — objectives render on the tactical map as flags (★ vital, ⚑ standard) with a capture-radius ring (color = owner, dashed = contested) and a blue/red control bar.

Theater v37 Jun 2026
Smoke / Obscurant System
Smoke clouds block line-of-sight — the primary LOS-denial tool in modern combat. Clouds block visual detection ~90% but thermal sensors only ~45% (models WP/RP smoke vs the rarer multispectral smoke). Shots crossing smoke lose accuracy; dense smoke (>70%) can fully block a shot.
On-board vehicle smoke dischargers — MBT/IFV/APC/Tank Destroyer pop a defensive smoke screen when pinned and taking fire (22s cooldown). Screens deploy toward the threat to break contact — exactly how real smoke grenade dischargers are used.
Artillery smoke missions — friendly artillery screens advancing infantry that are suppressed in the open, dropping smoke between the exposed unit and the nearest threat. Classic combined-arms screening.
Smoke physics — clouds grow to full radius, drift with wind, and dissipate over 9–18s. Thermal-capable shooters (tanks, ATGM, attack helis) see through smoke better than infantry. Rendered as billowing layered puffs, darker at night.
Counter-Battery Radar
Shoot-and-scoot is now mandatory — counter-battery radar (Firefinder / Zoopark) tracks artillery firing repeatedly from the same position. After 3 shots without displacing, a firing fix is achieved and enemy counter-fire is tasked onto that position after a short delay.
Displacement resets the fix — moving more than 6 world units between shots breaks the radar track (successful shoot-and-scoot). Artillery that holds position now gets destroyed by counter-fire — the real incentive that drives modern artillery TTPs.
Counter-fire strike — 45 damage, 12-unit splash, heavy suppression on the target battery. Weather degrades radar detection (rain/fog reduce track probability).
Aircraft Absolute Speeds
Jets and helicopters no longer move at the same speed — previously all aircraft shared the air TYPE base speed. Now absolute speeds: Interceptor 34, Fighter Jet 30, SEAD 28, Bomber 22, CAS 20, Drone 11, Attack Heli 10, Transport Heli 9. Jets transit the map fast; helicopters orbit locally — the correct order-of-magnitude difference.
Weather & Night Operations
Weather rolled each battle — 55% clear, then rain, fog, snow, storm. Visibility, detection range, and accuracy all scale with conditions. ~18% of battles are night engagements.
Weather grounds air ops — fog cuts air effectiveness to 55%, storms to 45%. CAS can't find targets in fog; unguided/optical weapons degrade far more than thermal/PGM (which barely care). Night degrades non-thermal shooters more (NV-equipped units like Spec-Ops, MBT, Attack Heli are less affected).
ERA & Warhead Types
HEAT vs APFSDS vs tandem — weapons now have a damage type. Explosive Reactive Armor (Kontakt-5 on MBTs) defeats 55% of single-charge HEAT (RPG, Hellfire, Maverick) but is bypassed by tandem warheads (Javelin, Kornet-E) and kinetic penetrators (APFSDS). Blast/HE is unaffected by ERA but poor vs armor anyway.
Practical effect — a Hellfire or RPG against an ERA-equipped MBT does roughly half damage; a Javelin's tandem charge punches through. This is why modern ATGMs went tandem and top-attack.
Bug Fixes & Cleanup
Structure firing-position range bonus wired — bunker/base range bonus was computed but never applied to effective range. Now correctly extends firing range for units in fortified positions. Removed two dead variables (srcRangeBonusMul, srcStruct) left over from v33.
Synthetic damage sources carry weapon type — kamikaze splash, inter-strike, and counter-battery applyDmg calls now pass a sub so the armor system resolves penetration correctly instead of falling back to a default.
Theater v36 Jun 2026
Armor Penetration System
Armor class per subtype (AC 0–3) — MBT: 3 (heavy), IFV/Tank Destroyer: 2 (medium), APC/HMMWV/recon: 1 (light), infantry/aircraft/supply: 0 (unarmored).
Armor penetration per weapon (AP 0–4) — small arms: 0, RPG/mortar: 1, autocannon/IFV: 2, ATGM/tank gun: 4, CAS/attack heli: 4, bombs: 2. Naval bypasses the land AP system.
Damage gating — AP ≥ AC: full damage. AP = AC−1: 35% (partial pen / deflection). AP ≤ AC−2: 8% (ricochet / spall only). Suppression is always applied regardless of penetration — a ricochet still pins infantry.
Practical effect — riflemen shooting an MBT do chip damage only; IFV autocannons partially dent heavy armor but can't kill efficiently; ATGM teams and tank guns are the primary armor killers. Blobs of light infantry can no longer attrition down MBTs.
Suppression System
Unit suppression state — every ground unit now tracks suppressed (bool), supTimer (decay countdown), supIntensity (0–1 severity), and pinned (hard movement block). Clears automatically after 3.5s without incoming fire.
Artillery suppression radius 18u — artillery, BML, and splash≥6 weapons suppress ALL ground enemies within 18 world units of the impact, even those not directly hit. Intensity falls off with distance. Morale drain 8/s at intensity 1.0.
Pinned units — when suppressed and morale <55, unit is pinned: cannot advance toward enemy (movement perpendicular component stripped), −22% accuracy, ×1.4 fire cooldown. Visual: orange pulsing halo. "PIN" label at close camera.
Suppression from all hits — direct fire hits also apply suppression (intensity 1.0 full pen, 0.5 partial, 0.2 ricochet). This makes heavy weapons like MGs effective suppressors even against armor they can't penetrate.
Attack Incentive
Stagnation penalty — ground units that don't advance (move <3 world units per check) accumulate a stagnation timer. Phase 1 (20–40s): mild morale drain 0.6/s. Phase 2 (40–60s): 1.4/s morale drain. Phase 3 (60s+): additional ammo drain 0.08/s (logistics cost of static lines). Cover halves penalties.
Harassment fire — every 18s, if the enemy has live artillery and the friendly side has a large static cluster, the enemy adjusts fire onto that cluster: suppression burst at centroid, morale drain, visual ring effects. Encourages breaking up static formations and advancing.
Cover reward — units inside bunkers/bases/ruins get 50% stagnation reduction (they have a tactical reason to hold). Routing units are exempt from stagnation (already penalised by routing system).

Theater v29 Jun 2026
RangeError: Maximum call stack size — root cause found
Exact location: hasLOS() at JS char 8635, col 23 inside stepDetection(). With 80+ units, the detection loop runs O(n²) = 6,400+ unit pairs per tick. Each pair calls calcDetection() → hasLOS() → 20× terrainH(). Total: ~128,000 function calls per detection cycle. On mobile, JavaScript engines have much smaller call stacks than desktop (typically 10,000–15,000 frames). The nested calls — stepDetection → calcDetection → hasLOS × 20 terrainH, repeated 6,400 times without yielding — exhausted the mobile call stack and threw RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
Fix 1 — LOS result cache. hasLOS(a,b) now caches results by unit ID pair in a Map, cleared each detection cycle. The pair (a→b) and (b→a) share the same entry. Across 6,400 pairs this reduces unique LOS computations to ~3,200 and eliminates redundant symmetric calls. Cache capped at 5,000 entries to bound memory.
Fix 2 — LOS ray steps reduced: 20 → 8. 20 terrain samples per ray was overengineered for a 60×36 grid at this scale. 8 steps gives the same practical blocking accuracy (terrain features are wide relative to step spacing) at 60% lower call depth.
Fix 3 — Detection pair cap: 800 per tick. stepDetection now breaks after 800 observer×target pairs per 0.25s cycle. Remaining pairs are checked on the next cycle. This spreads the O(n²) work across multiple ticks, preventing any single call from blowing the mobile stack. Detection quality is unchanged — all pairs are checked, just spread over 2–8 cycles for large engagements.
Fix 4 — vegetationPenalty steps: 12 → 6. Secondary call depth reduction in the vegetation sampling ray.
Theater v28 Jun 2026
Two Root Causes Fixed (confirmed by visual inspection)
Code visible at top — actual root cause (premature </style>). There were two </style> closing tags in the file. The first appeared immediately before the .struct-chip rules. The browser's HTML parser stops reading CSS at the first </style> and switches back to HTML rendering mode — everything after it (.struct-chip{...}, .struct-chip.base{...}, etc.) was treated as visible body text and rendered above the header. Fixed by removing the premature </style> so all rules stay inside a single stylesheet block.
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded — actual root cause (renderWiki recursive listener stacking). Inside renderWiki(), after writing el.innerHTML = h, the code called si.addEventListener('input', e => { ... renderWiki(); }). Every time renderWiki() ran it injected a fresh HTML search box and attached one more listener on top of any existing ones. After a handful of searches the element had dozens of stacked listeners, each calling renderWiki() which added more, until the call stack overflowed. Fixed by replacing addEventListener with si.oninput = ... — assignment replaces any previous handler rather than stacking. The callback also wraps renderWiki() in requestAnimationFrame() to yield to the browser between renders, preventing synchronous re-entry.
Theater v27 Jun 2026
Root Cause Fixes
Code visible at top — root cause found and fixed. The @media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) rule closing brace was on the same line as the start of the #hdr{display:flex...} rule, giving the CSS parser ...{animation:none}}display:flex.... The parser saw the second } as closing a non-existent outer block, then found display:flex as raw text outside any rule. Every CSS rule from #hdr onward was broken — elements rendered with browser defaults, #hdr became a plain block with its text content visible at the top of the page as raw "code". Fixed by inserting a newline between the media rule close and the #hdr{ opening.
RangeError — additional sources eliminated. The Math.max(...TKEYS.map(...)) in renderIntel was replaced with .reduce(). The drawRing3 function now clamps ellipse radii to [0.1, 500] before calling ctx.ellipse() — canvas throws an uncaught RangeError/DOMException when radius is NaN, Infinity, or negative, which occurred when rings from deep strikes or large explosions projected near the camera frustum edge. Added isFinite() guards on p.x, p.y, and a before any drawing call.
EW pulse ring radius guard. When EW vehicles have jamRadius=0 (non-EW units with the flag), psr=0 and arc(x,y,0) is technically valid but created visual artifacts. Now skipped when psr ≤ 1.
Deep strike ring missing r:0. The FX.rings.push in the deep strike VFX was missing the r:0 initialization field (all other ring pushes had it). stepFX computes r.r = r.max * (r.age/r.life) — without the initial field r.r was undefined for the first frame, causing the ellipse call to receive undefined * scale = NaN. Fixed.
Global render error guard. window.onerror now catches and logs any uncaught errors without crashing the browser tab. The draw() call in the main loop is wrapped in a try/catch — a single bad frame no longer freezes the entire simulation.

Bug Fixes
RangeError: invalid array length — fixed. Math.max(...array.map(...)) is called with spread syntax, which pushes every element as a function argument. JavaScript argument stacks have a limit (~65,535 entries). With 80+ units × sensors this blew the stack. Replaced all three sites (drawDetectionRings, morale encirclement spread, country power max) with .reduce() which uses no stack allocation.
Duplicate switch case — fixed. The v25 behavioral doctrine switch had case 'deep_battle' appear twice (once as a full block at line ~3516 and again as a fallthrough with cruise_salvo at ~3556). JavaScript switch executes the first matching case and ignores the second — the second block was dead code, and cruise_salvo fell through to nothing. Removed the duplicate; both doctrines now have their correct single blocks.
Orphaned switch cases — fixed. The sead_dead, cas_package, cap, lo_lo_lo, bvr_sweep, and strike_package cases were accidentally placed outside the switch {} body, making them unreachable dead code. Units using those doctrines fell through to default and used plain FSM movement. All cases merged back into the switch correctly.
BVR sweep fighter index — fixed. frUnits.indexOf(u) returns -1 for the current unit (since frUnits excludes u itself). Changed to frUnits.findIndex(f=>f.id===u.id) to get the correct slot index for line-abreast spacing.
Inline code tags in patch notes now styled — previously rendered as raw monospace blocks that looked like leaked code. Now display as small inline-highlighted tokens.
Performance
Detection rings throttled — were re-projecting 16 terrain points per unit per frame (~1,280 expensive calls at 80 units). Now throttled to every 5 frames (12fps). Per-unit rings only drawn when force ≤ 20 units; army envelope always shown. 12-point polygons instead of 16.
Morale auras throttled — throttled to every 3 frames (20fps). Gradient computation was happening every frame per alive unit.
C2 lines throttled — throttled to every 4 frames (15fps). Line drawing to every unit is expensive at scale.
Blitzkrieg filter caching — inner loop triple-computed frUnits.filter(f=>f.t==='veh') for every infantry unit every tick. Now computed once per blitz infantry unit using a cached filter result.
CAS package .filter().length → .some() — checking if any friendly CAS exists used filter().length > 0 which builds a full array. Replaced with .some() which short-circuits on first match.
Theater v25 Jun 2026
Behavioral Doctrine System
What changed — v24 tactics only modified stat multipliers (speed ×1.28, accuracy +0.10). Units still all moved and targeted the same way regardless of doctrine. v25 replaces the old 4-line movement patch with a full 14-doctrine behavioral movement system that controls WHERE units go, HOW they approach, and WHAT they target. Stats are secondary.
Blitzkrieg — vehicles drive in tight columns straight at the enemy centroid with minor lateral fan-out. Infantry phases 12–22u behind the vehicle wave. Artillery holds at standoff range and fires over the wave. You can see the armored spearhead forming and infantry following.
Mass Assault — every unit vectors toward the enemy centroid from a slightly different angle, creating a visible swarm convergence. At close range they pure-press on their individual targets. Separation radius is very tight (1.8u) so they pack densely.
Fire & Maneuver — units split by parity (odd/even ID). Every 2 seconds the bounding group switches. Half the force advances while the other half holds position and fires. Creates a visible leap-frog advance — you can watch units alternately move and shoot.
Defense in Depth — units self-organize into 4 depth rows based on unit ID. Row 0 holds at max range, row 1 at 1.3× range, row 2 at 1.6× range, row 3 even further back. Each row holds its line rather than advancing. Units micro-jitter laterally to use terrain cover.
Asymmetric — each unit approaches from a unique probe angle computed from its ID. During engagement phases (AMBUSH/OVERWATCH states) they hold completely still and fire. During movement phases they infiltrate from their unique angle. No massing — dispersed throughout the AO.
Precision — all units advance to maximum effective range and hold there. No charges. If a unit drifts inside optimal range it micro-pulls back. Standoff engagement until the target is destroyed.
Suppression Fire — artillery advances to mid-range and holds. Infantry bounds on a 2s on/2s off cycle staggered by unit row. You can watch waves of infantry moving while artillery fires overhead, then infantry halting while next wave bounds.
Deep Battle — BML/arty stays at maximum range and fires into the rear. Infantry and vehicles advance only enough to pin the enemy in place, jabbing laterally to maintain pressure without overcommitting. Simultaneous pressure at front and rear.
Attrition Warfare — units advance in a broad even front, each correcting lateral drift to stay in line with neighbors. Slow, methodical. No flanking, no rush. The line just grinds forward.
SEAD/DEAD Package — SEAD aircraft break from the group and go directly toward the nearest radar emitter (AA/EW unit). Escort fighters sweep for air contacts. Ground forces hold in place until SEAD clears the radars.
BVR Sweep — fighters form a line-abreast with equal spacing (8u gaps) and advance at BVR standoff range. Each fighter holds its lateral position in the sweep line. Ground forces hold back waiting for the sweep to clear.
CAP — fighters orbit at 1.4× effective range radius around the enemy centroid. Non-air units advance normally.
Low-Low-Low Strike — air units stagger laterally (4u spacing) before ingress to avoid line-abreast radar exposure. All head toward the target but from slightly different angles.
CAS Package — infantry and vehicles hold slightly back (inside 1.2× effective range) while CAS aircraft are alive. Infantry advances only when CAS is down or battle is late-phase.
Strike Package — bombers hold at 1.4× range in an orbit behind fighters. Fighters handle their own sweep FSM. Bombers only advance when a path is cleared.
Doctrine Targeting Changes
What units shoot at now depends on doctrine. Blitzkrieg: vehicles hunt soft targets first (supply, arty), then vehicles. Asymmetric: guerilla units prioritize logistics and EW. SEAD/DEAD: SEAD aircraft lock exclusively onto radar emitters. Deep Battle: BML targets arty/supply rear. BVR Sweep: fighters refuse to engage ground targets. CAS Package: CAS prioritizes armor. Precision: hunts high-HP command assets.

Named Air & Combined-Arms Tactics
16 named doctrines replacing the original 8. Each has a category (Air / Ground / Combined), a real-world doctrine reference, and specific mechanical modifiers. New doctrines:
SEAD/DEAD Package — mirrors Desert Storm Day 1, Kosovo, OIF. SEAD units get +20% ARM Pk. Fighters follow the gap. Triggers when enemy AA density is high.
BVR Fighter Sweep — US DCA/OCA sweep. All fighters prioritise air targets, crank aggressively after shot (+30% crank aggression). Air range +12%, accuracy +6%.
CAS Package — USMC MAGTF / AH-64 support integration. CAS Aircraft and Attack Helis get +8% acc and +10% speed. React time halved for ground attack runs.
Strike Package — B-52/F-15E Gulf War packages. Bombers target arty/logistics rear. Fighters escort the corridor. Bomber accuracy +10%.
CAP (Combat Air Patrol) — NATO Baltic CAP loiter. Fighters orbit at HIGH energy at +40% BVR range. React to any contact within sensor envelope.
Low-Low-Low Strike — Cold War NATO strike profile in SAM-saturated environment. All aircraft ingress at NOE. Higher MANPADS risk, lower SAM exposure. −6% accuracy penalty for flat trajectory.
Hi-Lo-Hi Strike — Post-Gulf War NATO standard. High ingress for fuel efficiency, NOE attack run, high egress. +4% accuracy, 15% fuel saving.
Suppression Fire — Soviet/Russian fire-and-move. Arty fires 20% faster at reduced accuracy ahead of infantry bounds. Combined advance rate 85% of normal.
Deep Battle — Tukhachevsky/AirLand Battle. BML/cruise missiles target enemy arty at +10% range. Front engages simultaneously. Mirrors 1991 Gulf War operational art.
Cruise Missile Salvo — Kalibr/Tomahawk saturation. BML fires first at max range, +15% Pk, 15% faster reload. Air follows. Triggers when BML launchers are available.
Attrition Warfare — WWI/Korea/Iran-Iraq. Accepts casualties for sustained firepower. +4% accuracy, −15% speed. High morale threshold required before routing.
Cruise Missile System
4 cruise missile subtypes added to BML: Kalibr 3M14 (Russian, CEP 2–3m, 1500km), Kh-101 (air-launched, CEP 5m, 5500km, low-RCS), Tomahawk BGM-109 (US, CEP <10m, 2500km), JASSM-ER (AGM-158B, CEP 2–3m, 980km, low-observable). All sourced from WEG Vol 2 Ch 2 and Jane's Strategic Weapon Systems.
Cruise vs ballistic differentiation — cruise missiles (⊸ glyph) fly lower, slower trajectories vs ballistic arcs (⊿). Cruise types have lower flight altitude, better CEP, and longer range. Ballistic types have higher splash and shorter response time.
BML subtype stats — each launcher now tracks type ('srbm'|'cruise'), CEP (metres), warhead mass, and real-world range in km for the Intel/Wiki display. Scud CEP 450m, Iskander CEP 2–5m, Kalibr CEP 2–3m, JASSM-ER CEP 2–3m.
Intel Tab — Tactics Tracker
Live tactic event log — every time either side's Adaptive Doctrine Engine changes tactic, an event is recorded in the Tactics Tracker with: timestamp (T+Xs), side, new tactic name, previous tactic, trigger reason, map position centroid of force, power ratio at time of switch, and active unit counts (air/veh/inf).
Filter by category — tracker has filter buttons: All · Blue · Red · Air · Ground · Combined. Events are color-coded by tactic category (purple=air, orange=ground, cyan=combined) and side (blue/red border).
80-event rolling buffer per battle. Tracker persists across the battle and is cleared on new battle start. Clear button available in Intel tab. Campaign record and battle history remain separate above the tracker.
Tracker updates in Intel tab every time renderIntel() is called — on battle end, on tab switch, and via the manual clear button.

Air-Only Modes
Air Superiority scenario — pure air war: 10 fighters + 4 drones + 2 EW per side, no ground forces at all. BVR engagements dominate early; WVR turning fights develop at close range. Win condition: destroy all enemy air. Scenario available in Mode selector.
Drone War scenario — mirrors Ukraine 2022–24 / Azerbaijan–Armenia 2020: both sides field large UAS forces (14–18 drones) with small fighter screens and dense EW. No traditional ground forces. EW jamming is decisive — Shaheds die to Bukovel-AD analogs. Available in Mode selector.
Deep Drone System
Drone subtypes differentiated — Kamikaze Dove (Shahed-136 analog): slow, NOE/LOW altitude, RCS 0.008m², 72% EW vulnerability, no air-to-air capability, terminal dive on contact. Strike UAS (Orion/TB-2 analog): orbits at MID altitude, carries 2 precision munitions, 35% EW vulnerability, can fire AGM at ground targets.
EW anti-drone disruption — enemy EW jammers within 1.6× radius actively attack drone guidance: 72% per-second disruption chance on loitering munitions (GPS/datalink dependent), 35% on strike UAS. Disrupted Kamikazes detonate harmlessly (60% chance) or wander randomly. Strike UAS loses lock and orbits aimlessly for 3–8s. Models Bukovel-AD, SHORAD EW effects from Ukraine.
Drone FSM rewrite — Kamikaze Dove: TRANSIT → terminal dive when close, wanders when EW-disrupted. Strike UAS: high-altitude orbit → fire AGM at ground targets → continue orbit. Both check disruption state each tick.
ISR bonus from UAS — alive Strike UAS extend friendly sensor range by +18% each (max +54% for 3 UAS). Models the ISR/targeting support of persistent UAS like TB-2, Orion, Bayraktar.
Air-to-Ground Pk System
8 weapon type Pk tables — each with per-target-type Pk values from real-world data: PGM (Pk 0.82–0.90 vs vehicle), Maverick AGM (0.88), Hellfire/Vikhr ATGM (0.91), loitering munition (0.65), rockets (0.18 vs veh), unguided bombs (0.12 vs veh), cannon strafing (0.055 vs veh, 0.38 vs inf), cluster munition (0.22 vs veh, 0.65 vs inf open).
Weapon mapping per subtype — CAS Aircraft fires rockets primary; Attack Heli fires Hellfire/Vikhr; Strike UAS fires Maverick-class; Bomber drops unguided; SEAD uses PGM+ARM; Fighter uses PGM; Kamikaze Dove is loitering munition impact.
Target hardness modifiers — armoured vehicles are inherently harder to kill: hardness factor 1.0 for veh/inf, 1.1 for arty (armour protection). Supply trucks and EW vehicles softer (0.85–0.90). Naval targets hardest at 0.60 (ship survivability).
Environmental Pk degradation — forest/urban cover: −0.10 Pk. Moving target: −0.08. EW-disrupted shooter: ×0.35 (massive accuracy loss when jammed). Altitude modifier: NOE is −0.08 (flat trajectory), MID optimal (+0.06), very high −0.05 (unguided accuracy degrades at slant range).
Strike call events — each A2G weapon release logs to the event feed: "Hellfire away", "PGM impact", "Gun run", "Bombs away", "Terminal impact" etc, with shooter subtype, target subtype, and Pk. Rate-limited to 3.5s per aircraft to avoid spam.
Area weapon splash — unguided bombs (8u splash), cluster munitions (12u splash), and rockets (4u splash) deal reduced damage to nearby units when they hit, modeling real area-of-effect lethality patterns.
Theater v22 Jun 2026
Deep Air Combat System
AAM loadouts per subtype — Fighter Jet: R-77/AIM-120 BVR (×4) + R-73/AIM-9 WVR (×4) + guns. Interceptor: R-37M VLRAAM BVR (68u range, ×4) + R-73 WVR (×2). SEAD: Kh-31P/HARM ARM (×4) + self-defense IR. CAS: no BVR, IR WVR (×2) + heavy cannon. Attack Heli: ATGM-AA WVR (×8) + 30mm. Each shot type tracked separately.
Realistic Pk model — every AAM shot uses a multi-factor probability calculation (validated against T-001 through T-020 test records in THEATER_AirCombat_Tests.md): base Pk from real-world assessment × aspect modifier × altitude advantage × EW jam modifier × fatigue modifier × range degradation. ARH BVR ~0.52, IR WVR tail ~0.73, gun burst ~0.055 — all within validated test bands.
Aspect angle mechanics — aspectAngle(shooter,target) computes degrees off-tail. BVR ARH: head-on gives +0.08 Pk (high closure). WVR IR: tail-aspect gives +0.14 Pk (max IR signature). Beam/oblique angles reduce Pk on both.
Altitude advantage — each altitude tier above the target adds ±0.18 Pk. Shooting down = positive energy for missile. Shooting up = kinematic disadvantage. MiG-31 at HIGH vs bomber at LOW gets full +0.18.
RWR (Radar Warning Receiver) — radar-guided AAM launches set a 4-second radar lock on the target. Locked units display a red !! indicator and are pushed into defensive FSM states: NOTCH (beam to radar notch), DRAG (run cold to drain missile energy), or DEFENSIVE (break turn). 35% chance per second of entering defensive state when locked.
Chaff/flare countermeasures — each air subtype has a type-appropriate CM inventory (Attack Heli: 8 chaff / 30 flares; Fighter: 24 chaff / 16 flares). Auto-deployed on RWR warning. Chaff vs SARH: 65% miss. Chaff vs ARH: 48% miss (+15% if notching). Flares vs IR (non-IRCCM): 60% miss. All within T-008–T-010 validated bands.
Fox calls in event feed — each AAM launch logs "Fox-1 (SARH)", "Fox-2 (IR)", "Fox-3 (ARH)", "Fox-3 (VLRAAM)", "ARM away", or "Fox-4 (guns)" with shooter subtype, target subtype, and range. Rate-limited to 3s between calls per aircraft to avoid spam.
BVR crank geometry — Fighter Jets in INTERCEPT state perform a BVR crank (angle 30° off boresight at missile range) to hold radar lock while reducing own exposure to a return shot. After shot, they can go cold (DRAG) or press to merge.
SEAD ARM effectiveness — Kh-31P/HARM launches check if target is a valid radar emitter (arty, ew, AA subtype). ARM Pk: 0.62 base, applies vs radar-emitting targets only. Non-emitting targets ignored entirely — forces player to prioritize SEAD against active radars.
Test records — 20 real-world validation tests in THEATER_AirCombat_Tests.md covering AAM Pk, CM effectiveness, historical scenario matching, altitude effects, and EW integration. 17/20 pass, 3/20 marginal, 0 fail.
Theater v21 Jun 2026
Critical Fix — Map Restored
Map disappeared (root cause) — the v20 CSS edit deleted the original #app{display:grid} rule and replaced it at line 315, AFTER the @media(max-width:900px) block. In Claude's artifact iframe the viewport is narrow, so the media query fired and the 44vh mid-row left the canvas zero-height after layout. Fixed by placing the base #app grid rule first in CSS, before any media queries, and restructuring breakpoints so they never zero out the map area.
Detection crash — hasLOS() and calcDetection() called terrainH() and terrainTypeAt() with undefined terrain during the first tick before buildTerrain() completed. Added HEIGHT.length guards and wrapped stepDetection in a try/catch so detection errors can never crash the render loop.
New — Fatigue System
Unit fatigue (0–100) — all combat units accumulate fatigue from sustained contact and movement. Fatigue rate varies by type: aircraft 0.20/s, vehicles 0.14/s, infantry 0.08/s, arty 0.06/s. Rest recovery: 1.5/s when out of contact range.
Fatigue penalties — each fatigue point applies: −0.3% accuracy, −0.2% speed, +0.15% fire cooldown, −0.02/s morale recovery. At fatigue ≥80 (exhausted) units may randomly halt. At ≥95 (breaking) units rout regardless of morale.
Fatigue bar — orange bar renders above the HP bar when fatigue >20. Turns bright orange above 80 (exhausted). Visible when zoomed in.
New — Deep EW System
EW Deception — units near enemy jammers (within 1.4× jam radius) suffer a 35% additional sensor range reduction beyond basic jamming. EW vehicles now project a "deception zone" in addition to jamming.
Comms Blackout — when 2+ friendly EW units overlap their jam zones, the overlap area becomes a blackout zone. Enemy C2 HQ integrity drains 3× faster inside blackout zones, stacking with other disruption sources.
EW Burnthrough — if a unit is illuminated by 3+ friendly sensors simultaneously, jamming is 50% overcome (burned through). Large recon/sensor formations can push through dense EW.
New — Surgical Deep Strike System
5 strike types per side (2 uses each, per engagement) available in the C2 tab: C2 HQ Strike (destroys HQ integrity), Supply Strike (−40% enemy ammo/fuel), Counter-Battery (precision arty kill), EW Burnout (suppresses all enemy jammers 20s), Air Intercept (destroys highest-threat enemy air unit).
Visual strike effect — each deep strike spawns a ballistic arc and explosion ring at the target location, giving clear visual feedback of where the strike landed.
Cooldowns and limits — each strike type has its own cooldown (20–40s) and per-engagement use count. Strike buttons show remaining uses and cooldown timer. Disabled when on cooldown or uses exhausted.
Theater v20 Jun 2026
Bug Fixes
createRadialGradient crash — actually fixed — v19 guarded on R<2 but the real crash was p.x / p.y being NaN or Infinity when units project off the visible frustum. Added isFinite(p.x) && isFinite(p.y) check before drawing, plus a try/catch around the gradient call to prevent any remaining edge cases from crashing the render loop.
Fullscreen black screen — actually fixed — v19 tried requestFullscreen() on document.documentElement. This causes the browser to fullscreen the entire viewport outside the CSS grid context, so #app lost its size and the canvas got zeroed. Reverted to CSS-class-only fullscreen: toggling body.fsmap collapses the side panels via grid 0 1fr 0 columns, then calls resize() 230ms later after the transition completes. No native fullscreen API — no black screen.
Attack Plan close button — actually fixed — the plan canvas (z-index:11) was sitting above the plan panel (z-index:14 in v19, but still intercepting clicks because pointer-events:all covered the whole #mid). Fixed by: (1) raising plan panel to z-index:16, (2) adding e.target.closest('#planPanel') check in _planDown so clicks on panel buttons pass through to their handlers, (3) removed the SIM.running guard from openPlanMode so it opens any time.
Plan mode blue/red differentiation — tool selection buttons now correctly highlight with blue-on / red-on / obj-on CSS classes. Arrows draw labeled "BLUE AXE" or "RED AXE" in the correct color with glow. Objectives render as ⊕ (blue) or ⊛ (red) with side-colored pulsing rings. The panel explains each tool's mechanical effect inline.
Theater v19 Jun 2026
Detection & Line of Sight System
Sensor profiles — every unit now has sensor (visual, thermal, radar, sigint) and signature (visual, thermal, radar, acoustic) values tuned per unit type. Infantry: high visual, low radar. Tanks: high thermal signature and radar. Drones: broad sensor coverage. EW vehicles: radar sensor, low signature.
Detection calculation — each tick, observers check enemies using calculateDetection(): range factor × terrain visibility factor × stealth factor × EW suppression factor × LOS factor. Result is a probability 0–1. If random roll passes, target becomes spotted=true.
Line-of-sight raycasting — hasLOS(a,b) marches 20 steps along the ray, sampling terrain height. Blocked if terrain exceeds the interpolated sight line. Flying units always have LOS. EW units elevate their effective eye height.
Terrain visibility modifiers — plains 1.0, hills 0.85, forest 0.45, urban 0.30, jungle 0.20, mountain 0.50, swamp 0.60, tundra 0.90, desert 1.05.
Vegetation/cover line penalty — sampling the ray for forest/urban tiles adds cumulative opacity. Dense jungle corridors can reduce detection to 0.
Contact decay — unspotted units age their contactAge each tick. After 25s without detection, lastKnownPos clears. Units fire toward last known position for 8 seconds before losing the contact entirely.
Fire control gating — units can only fire at targets that are spotted OR within melee range (≤5 units). This gates the entire combat loop: undetected units do not take fire.
Detection radius visualization — toggle "◎ Detection Radius" (map overlay) to see the maximum visual sensor range of all alive units as colored rings (blue/red). Ring opacity shows unit density. The combined army detection bubble is shown as a larger faint envelope.
Attack Plan Mode — Reworked
Floating plan panel — replaced broken centered toolbar with a left-side floating panel that stays out of the way of the 3D view. Opens/closes cleanly.
Blue vs Red arrows clearly differentiated — Blue arrows: blue dashed with blue glow labeled "BLUE AXE". Red arrows: red dashed with red glow labeled "RED AXE". Clicking the matching button selects that tool; active tool is highlighted.
Objectives explained in UI — each objective type (Blue Obj / Red Obj) has an inline note explaining what it does mechanically: units prioritize targets near own objectives, and the objective pulls unit movement.
Touch support for plan drawing — touch events on planCanvas now work for drawing on mobile/tablet and landscape phone mode.
Bug Fixes
createRadialGradient crash — inner radius was R*0.2 which could equal or exceed outer radius when R was very small. Now inner radius is always 0 and guarded with R>2 before calling gradient.
Fullscreen — now uses native requestFullscreen() API on the #app element. Falls back to fsmap CSS class. Also handles fullscreenchange events to keep button state synced when the browser exits fullscreen natively (Escape key).
Screen rotation / landscape — added orientationchange listener that calls resize() with 300ms delay. Added landscape media query that collapses side panels and gives the map full screen on phones.

Theater v16 Jun 2026
Command & Control Chain Integration
C2 Chain architecture — each side now has a hierarchical command structure: Commander (top level) → 3 Division HQs (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie) → unit groups. HQs are virtual nodes with integrity 0–100. Each HQ tracks the units assigned to its division and its current disruption state.
C2 Integrity — overall C2 integrity is the mean HQ integrity weighted by divisional unit count. Full integrity (100%) has no effect. Degraded integrity introduces order-delay penalties, accuracy penalties, and formation-shift suppression. At <20% a side cannot adapt doctrine or formation at all — the AI is effectively blinded.
Order propagation delay — when tactical orders are issued, each unit's order now applies after a delay proportional to (1 − C2 integrity). Full C2: ~0s lag. 50% integrity: up to 4s lag. Below 25%: up to 8s lag. Units show a pending state until the order lands.
HQ disruption mechanics — HQs can be disrupted by: (a) EW units within jamming radius (continuous low-grade disruption), (b) artillery splash landing near the HQ centroid of assigned units, (c) player-triggered C2 strike via the C2 panel. Disrupted HQs impose a morale drain on their division's units (+0.8/s morale loss) and a −10% accuracy penalty.
C2 Strike (player action) — from the C2 tab, each side can issue a targeted C2 Strike against one of the enemy's three HQs once per engagement. The strike instantly reduces that HQ to 0 integrity. HQs regenerate at 8 integrity/s from partial disruption, but a full strike takes 18s to recover. Strike button has a 25s cooldown after use.
HQ restoration (player action) — per-side Restore button attempts to rally a disrupted friendly HQ back to 60% integrity immediately. Can be used once per HQ per battle. Simulates rapid re-establishment of comms/staff.
Adaptation lockout — the Adaptive Doctrine Engine's tactic/formation recommender now checks C2 integrity before committing a switch. If integrity <30%, the switch is silently blocked (logged as "C2 degraded — adaptation suppressed"). This models how disrupted command prevents timely doctrinal pivots.
C2 panel (right panel → C2 tab) — live display of both sides' C2 chains: overall integrity bar (green/amber/red), per-HQ status with unit count and disruption state, C2 event log (strikes, disruptions, restorations), and action buttons (C2 Strike, Restore HQ). Panel updates every 6 frames like the Live tab.
Accuracy coupling — units assigned to a disrupted HQ fire with reduced accuracy. Disrupted HQ: −12% base accuracy modifier applied per unit in that division each tick. Stacks with EW jamming (but independently).
C2 events in feed — HQ disruptions, strikes, and restorations generate entries in the bottom event feed and the C2 event log in the panel.
Reset handling — C2 state resets fully on battle start: all HQ integrity back to 100, all events cleared, strike/restore flags cleared.
Theater v15 Jun 2026
Features
Adaptive Doctrine Engine — every 12 simulation seconds, each side's AI evaluates battlefield performance and may switch doctrine or formation. Evaluation uses: power momentum (Δ power ratio over the interval), arty pressure (own units with degraded morale from splash), suppression exposure, enemy composition, own composition, morale average, routing count, and spread score (spatial dispersion of own units).
Doctrine switching rules — 15+ weighted conditions drive doctrine selection. Examples: losing power ratio ≥ 1.5→ → press with Blitzkrieg/Mass; ratio < 0.7 → Defense/Asymmetric; enemy has strong arty → close fast with Blitzkrieg; enemy has air superiority → contest with Airpower; low morale → stabilise with Defense; negative momentum for 2 intervals → penalise current doctrine and explore alternatives. Novelty pressure discourages loops. 1.5-interval cooldown after each switch.
Formation switching rules — 8+ conditions. Doctrine-formation affinity table (e.g. Blitzkrieg → Wedge/Column; Defense → Box/Refused Flank; Asymmetric → Dispersed). Enemy arty/drones → dispersed. Winning by large margin → Pincer envelopment. Losing badly → Box to protect remaining forces. Unit spread too tight/loose → rebalance.
Live formation migration — when a formation is adopted mid-battle, each unit receives a migration target position (fmTgtX/Y) and stepFormationMigration() nudges them toward it at 30% of unit speed each tick. Units blend formation repositioning with their normal behaviour FSM — no teleporting.
Adaptive emphasis targeting — after each evaluation the engine identifies the most threatening enemy arm (vehicles×2, air×3, arty×2.5) and sets emphasisType. All units on that side gain a 45% range-score discount when targeting that type, effectively concentrating fire without overriding individual behaviour.
Doctrine AI panel — Live tab shows real-time Doctrine AI status for both sides: current tactic, formation, momentum arrow (▲/▼/◎), emphasis arm, adapting/holding badge, and last 3 adaptation decisions with timestamps.
Adaptation history log — each doctrine and formation change is logged with sim-time and reason string (e.g. "Precision Strike → Blitzkrieg (pressing advantage)", "Box → Dispersed (arty pressure)") visible in the Live panel and the feed.
Theater v14 Jun 2026
Mechanics
AA-only air engagement — removed triangle doctrine (inf>air>veh>inf). Aircraft and drones can now ONLY be engaged by designated AA units: MANPADS, AA Vehicle, AA Battery, Fighter Jet, Interceptor, SEAD Aircraft, Missile Cruiser, Destroyer, Frigate — plus any subtype with dmgOver.air ≥ 2. Everything else ignores flying targets entirely.
Deep tactic modifiers — 8 doctrines now each modify tacRanMul, tacStandoff, tacClose, tacSpdMul, tacAccMod, tacFireMul, tacSplMul independently per unit type. E.g. Blitzkrieg: vehicles sprint at 1.35× but arty fires rapidly at reduced range; Defense: infantry gets +13% accuracy on high ground, arty splash ×1.20; Mass: fire rate ×1.33 with −4% accuracy; Asymmetric: infantry takes dispersed jitter angle approach. Country-specific overlays on top (Israel precision +5% acc, GER blitzkrieg veh +8% spd, PRK mass fire rate ×1.10).
Doctrine-driven movement geometry — Asymmetric infantry takes jitter approach angles (hard to suppress). Blitzkrieg vehicles cut straight through (Y-damped). Defense doctrine stops ground units from advancing when already in effective range. Separation radii and weights tuned per doctrine (mass: tight 1.8 units; asymmetric: loose 6.5 units; blitzkrieg: loose column 2.5 units).
Priority-based targeting (no triangle) — acquire() now scores targets by: threat (enemy targeting you = 0.4×), role value (supply 0.3×, BML 0.25×, EW 0.5×), subtype doctrine (interceptors ignore ground, SEAD hunts AA, tank destroyers hunt MBTs, CAS hunts ground), and tactic (precision prefers high-HP targets, mass prefers close range). Supply trucks remain top-priority soft targets.
Completed BML system — ballistic missile launchers added to OOB (max 4 per side), FORCE defaults include them. BML subtypes: Scud-B, DF-15B, Iskander-M, Fateh-313. Splash radius 16–22 units. All fire ballistic arcing FX with re-entry heating glow. LOGI ammo drain 30% per shot — very ammo-limited.
Tactical orders fully wired — 8 orders (Hold, Charge, Leapfrog, Withdraw, Flank Left/Right, Concentrate, Suppress) apply per-unit override to behaviour FSM. Suppress order reduces fire cooldown by 30%. Orders panel renders in Live tab with per-side buttons and recent order log.
Bug Fixes
Splash damage now hits all unit types — removed the old e.t!=='inf' filter that blocked artillery splash from hitting vehicles. All units in radius are now damaged.
tacAccMod correctly stored on unit and read in fireAt (was calculated but never applied in v13).
orderCdMul logic — fixed the !orderBres===false tautology; suppress order now correctly passes its cdMulOverride.
Theater v13 Jun 2026
Features (v13, incomplete)
Ballistic Missile Launchers (partial) — BML type added to TYPES and SUBTYPES. Behaviour FSM: DEPLOY→READY→FIRE→DISPLACE to avoid counter-battery. Ballistic arc tracer with parabola, re-entry glow, and impact ring.
Tactical Orders (partial) — 8 mid-battle orders; applyOrderOverride() FSM override. Orders panel HTML and renderOrdersUI().
Intermittent off-map strikes — Missile Defence scenario fires random ballistic tracers from off-screen that deal splash damage on impact. stepFX() processes impact on tracer completion.
Theater v12 Jun 2026
New Scenarios
Country vs Country — default free-play mode. Full manual control of both sides. No restrictions.
Drone Swarm Attack — USA (AA/EW heavy) defends against Iranian kamikaze drone waves. Waves spawn every 20s up to 5 waves, each larger than the last. BLUE wins by surviving 90s with >40% power; RED wins by breaking the defence.
Missile Defence — Israel (air/intercept heavy) counters a North Korean mass artillery + aircraft saturation strike. BLUE must destroy RED launch platforms; RED wins by collapsing BLUE supply/power.
Base Defence — US professional force in box formation holds against a Syrian mass-infantry insurgent assault. High morale asymmetry — attacker numbers vs defender discipline.
Hardpoint Assault — Russia (blitzkrieg wedge) storms a German-held fortified ridge in refused-flank formation. Attacker must break through in 90s; defender holds with arty support.
Naval & Air — flat ocean map, naval and air units only. US vs China task force engagement: destroyers, frigates, submarines, and carrier aircraft. Torpedoes, missiles, and AA dominate. No ground forces permitted.
Features
Scenario selector panel — new UI section above Engagement with one-click scenario buttons showing glyph, name, and detailed description with tags. Scenarios auto-configure force compositions and doctrines.
Naval map — flat ocean terrain with a small island group. All cells biome as Water/Coast. Replaces standard heightmap when any naval scenario is active. "New Terrain" button respects naval mode.
Custom win conditions — each scenario has a tailored victory condition checked each tick (power thresholds, time limits, asset destruction). Standard last-unit-standing is the fallback.
Drone wave spawner — Drone Swarm scenario dynamically spawns RED drone waves mid-battle at 20s intervals, each wave larger than the last, from the RED deployment edge.
Scenario victory messages — win banner shows scenario-specific description (e.g. "Swarm repelled", "Hardpoint held") instead of generic "Blue victory".
Theater v11 Jun 2026
Bug Fixes
Icons clipping into terrain — ground unit icons now projected at terrain height + 2.5 world-unit hover offset (ICON_HOVER). Icons given depth-sort bias of −1.0 so they always render above terrain tiles.
Force proximity — spawn clamped: BLUE max 48% map-X, RED min 52%, guaranteed no overlap at any unit count.
Features
Deep morale system (20+ inputs) — Drains: damage (proportional to HP lost), death contagion, suppression, encirclement arc detection, isolation, routing witness, ammo/fuel critical, unfavourable terrain. Recovery: vet rate, supply truck, cohesion, victory momentum, high ground, cover terrain, formation cohesion, leadership (vet-near-vet), ally kill witness, doctrine bonus.
Doctrine morale modifiers — Defense +0.25/s, Blitzkrieg +0.20/s, Combined Arms/Maneuver +0.15/s, Mass −0.10/s.
Terrain morale effects — Mountain/Forest/Urban give cover bonus; Desert/Swamp drain morale from harsh conditions.
High morale combat bonus — morale > 80 gives +6% accuracy and +10% speed. Low morale (< 25) gives −40% accuracy and +55% fire cooldown.
Surrender mechanic — routing units whose morale stays below 5 for 3+ seconds surrender (removed, counted as loss, event logged).
Field promotion system — units accumulating 80 XP from kills earn veteran status mid-battle with a morale/accuracy boost.
Rally cap degradation — each rally reduces a unit's morale cap by 5. Shattered units cannot recover to full strength.
Patch notes updated — full v2–v11 history in this drawer.

Depot-anchored spawn — units spawn clustered around their depot, guaranteed far-side separation.
Ridged mountain terrain — 5-octave ridged noise + Math.pow contrast exaggeration creates dramatic peaks and valleys.
Morale system v1 — per-unit morale, routing, death contagion, suppression. Deepened in v11.

Differentiated projectiles — 9 visual types: bullet, shell, missile, ATGM, bomb, rocket, laser, AA missile, torpedo — each with distinct motion, colour, and lifetime.

Features
Per-unit FSM behaviour system — 30+ states across all unit subtypes. CAS runs attack passes, helicopters pop-up and hover-fire, bombers loiter in orbit, snipers stalk then relocate, MBTs do bounding overwatch, arty displaces after each fire mission.
